family: The Chassidus Unity Index: Chassidus is one point
title: Chassidus Unity Index
abstract: The claim is the Lubavitcher Rebbe's. In Inyanah Shel Toras HaChassidus (1965) he says that Chassidus is "one point, not composed of distinct details": the Essence of God, drawn down and present in everything. Put as unity, that point reads "there is nothing besides Him", true even in the lowest earth, and that is His dwelling below. The Mitteler Rebbe says the same of his father's whole teaching, about 1821.

family: The Chassidus Unity Index: Chassidus is one point
title: The spine of the Chassidus Unity Index
abstract: The index's claim: Chassidus is not 220 books but one idea in 220 ways. This file sets out what that idea is, according to the Rebbeim themselves, the twelve faces it takes across the corpus, and the grammar by which any subject is shown to be one of those faces. It also says where the claim is the Rebbeim's own, where it is ours, and where it is thin.

family: The Chassidus Unity Index: Chassidus is one point
title: Subjects of Chassidus — for the Unity Index
abstract: Each subject below is to be traced back to one idea: the unity of God. This file is the subject list only. The passages come in the next stage. 197 subjects in 16 clusters. Tie to the unity: stated 129 · reading 60 · thin 8. How the list was made. It draws on the 22 pillars of Chassidus Concepts/ (each README and architecture, with their rooms and fault lines), 00_CONCEPT_MAP.md, 00_ATLAS.md and 00_LIBRARY_BY_CONCEPT.md, and on the four themes of the Sefer HaArachim synthesis (Achdus, Ohr/Tzimtzum, Osiyos, Human Avodah).

family: The Chassidus Unity Index: Chassidus is one point
title: Eight sources on the unity of God: what they say together
abstract: Each book says the one idea: there is nothing but God. Each also sees something the others do not. The Tanya says it from the person's side. The soul is a part of Him, the struggle is where He is hidden, and the deed is where He is held. Its test is a life. The two Gates say it from His side. The Essence is alone after creation as before, the hiding is His own power and only toward us, and opposites meet in Him.

family: 197 subjects in 16 clusters, each shown as a face of the one idea
title: K01 · God: Unity and Essence
abstract: These thirteen subjects are the one idea itself, seen from thirteen sides. No subject here needs to be connected to the unity from outside, because each is a way the sources say it. What separates them is which side they say it from: the name of the unity (S001-S002), its bearer (S003-S004), its exclusivity (S005), its two directions (S006-S007), its creative power (S008-S009, S012), its knowledge and care (S010-S011), and its purpose (S013).

family: 197 subjects in 16 clusters, each shown as a face of the one idea
title: K02 · Tzimtzum, Light and the Chain of Worlds
abstract: The claim of this cluster. Tzimtzum, light and the chain of worlds are the part of Chassidus where the one idea is most exposed to being misread as its opposite. They seem to be a map of God's distance from the world: a withdrawal, a void, a ladder of worlds, screens. The sources read every element of that map as the unity itself, seen from below. The contraction hides only toward the creatures (SH 6:8). The trace in the void holds all of Him in hint (Shaar HaYichud 13:55).

family: 197 subjects in 16 clusters, each shown as a face of the one idea
title: K03 · Sefiros, Names and the Supernal Order
abstract: These twelve subjects are the supernal order: the sefiros, their parts, their names and the will beneath them. A system of emanations looks like the opposite of a single point, since it has ten measures, partzufim, unions and names. The sources' answer, stated again and again, is that the order is the unity itself, spread into measures: 'He, His life and His vessels are one' (IH 20; Shaar HaYichud 27, 33).

family: 197 subjects in 16 clusters, each shown as a face of the one idea
title: K04 · Holiness, Kelipah and the Sparks
abstract: The moral cosmos of Chassidus (holiness, the husks, the permitted middle, the sparks) looks at first like a dualism: two sides at war. Read against the spine, every one of these subjects is defined by its relation to the one idea, and the sources say so in so many words. Holiness is what is nullified to Him (Tanya 6:5). Kelipah is what is not nullified and stands as a separate thing, living from the back of His will (Tanya 6:7, 22).

family: 197 subjects in 16 clusters, each shown as a face of the one idea
title: K05 · The Soul
abstract: These twelve subjects are the soul. Here the one idea turns inward: the Essence that is present in everything is present in a person in a special way, as 'a part of God above, literally', breathed from His inwardness (Tanya 2), and at its innermost point, the yechidah, 'always united with the Essence' and giving 'no room to anything besides Him' (Inyanah 11:5, 14:1). The rest of the anthropology follows from where that point stands. The divine soul's nature is bitul (Tanya 19).

family: 197 subjects in 16 clusters, each shown as a face of the one idea
title: K06 · Faculties of the Soul
abstract: The faculties of the soul look like a psychology: ten powers, a mind and a heart, a will, a delight, three garments. Read against the spine, they turn out to be the Chabad instrument for thinking the unity at all. The Alter Rebbe builds the analogy of creation out of them: one word is as nothing before the soul that speaks, as the world before Him (Tanya 20; 33:2).

family: 197 subjects in 16 clusters, each shown as a face of the one idea
title: K07 · Torah, Letters and the Study of Chassidus
abstract: These thirteen subjects are the Torah and the study of it. Here the one idea turns from things to words. If nothing exists besides Him, then what He says is not separate from Him. The Torah is 'His wisdom and will', and He and His wisdom are one (Tanya 4:5), so a person who knows a halachah holds His will in his mind in 'a wondrous union with no parallel' (Tanya 5:6).

family: 197 subjects in 16 clusters, each shown as a face of the one idea
title: K08 · Mitzvos
abstract: The mitzvot look like a legal code: 613 commands, each with its own measure, time and object. Read against the spine, the sources treat each mitzvah as a single act in which the unity becomes actual (F10), and the cluster shows it from three sides. First, the mitzvah as such is a bond. The Maharash says the creation of the worlds is 'only a mere radiance', whereas 'through the mitzvot there is a tzavta and joining with the Essence of Or Ein Sof' (Toras Shmuel 5627).

family: 197 subjects in 16 clusters, each shown as a face of the one idea
title: K09 · Prayer and Contemplation
abstract: These eleven subjects are the service of the heart. Here the one idea stops being described and is enacted. If there is nothing besides Him, prayer cannot be one self petitioning another; the sources rebuild it as the essence of the soul joining the Essence of Ein Sof ('to Him and not to His attributes', Hayom Yom 11 Tishrei). It draws 'the light itself', which alone is omnipotent, into the created world (Kuntres Acharon 4), and joins the filling light to the surrounding light (the Rebbe, 10 Shevat 5730).

family: 197 subjects in 16 clusters, each shown as a face of the one idea
title: K10 · Love, Awe, Cleaving and Bitul
abstract: These thirteen subjects are the inner life of the service: love, awe, the yoke, cleaving, the rhythm of running and returning, fervor, bitul and its opposite, humility, self-sacrifice and truth. In this cluster the one idea shows as the person's answer to it. If there is nothing besides Him, then love is possible only 'from the side of the unity' (Sha'arei Avodah, Introduction 5), and 'the first foundation of what arouses love and awe is faith in His unity' (Chinukh Katan 12).

family: 197 subjects in 16 clusters, each shown as a face of the one idea
title: K11 · Teshuvah and Refining Character
abstract: These thirteen subjects are the moral life seen from the one idea. If there is nothing besides Him, then sin cannot be a private debt between two parties. Tanya defines it as separation from His unity, like idolatry, because it opposes 'the will that gives life to all' (Tanya 24; IT 5). Teshuvah is then the soul's return to where it was one with Him before it was breathed out (IT 8).

family: 197 subjects in 16 clusters, each shown as a face of the one idea
title: K12 · Inner Life: Joy, Suffering, Faith and Death
abstract: These twelve subjects are the one idea as it is lived from inside: felt (joy, sadness, bitterness), suffered (suffering, trials), held (faith, trust, simplicity), lost and regained (doubt, despair and hope), and met at the edge (death, reward and punishment). The spine anchors only one of them in so many words (G16: joy in faith in the unity, Tanya 33), but the sources state far more. Iggeret HaKodesh 11 is the hinge of the cluster.

family: 197 subjects in 16 clusters, each shown as a face of the one idea
title: K13 · Time: Shabbos, Festivals and Months
abstract: These thirteen subjects are time itself seen from the one idea. Shaar HaYichud 7 puts time on the created side: a 'world' is space and time, both brought from nothing at every moment by His Malchus, both nullified before the Essence, and yet 'though above space and time He is found below in space and time' (SH 7:4-9). The calendar is then a pattern in which that unity is lived. Day and night are 'one day', the model for 'know that Havayah is Elokim' (LT Vaetchanan 7).

family: 197 subjects in 16 clusters, each shown as a face of the one idea
title: K14 · The Tzaddik and the Community
abstract: These eleven subjects are the one idea as a community. They start with one person in whom the yesh has become ayin (the tzaddik), run through the lines that bind souls to him and to Moshe, and reach the body of Israel as one stature, the couple, the child, the peace between opposites, the table of friends, and the teaching carried outward. The spine judged the doctrine of the tzaddik 'thin / forced' (pillar map, 03). This pass revises that for the tzaddik himself.

family: 197 subjects in 16 clusters, each shown as a face of the one idea
title: K15 · Exile, Redemption, the Nations and the Land
abstract: These twelve subjects are the one idea read along history and geography. The spine's F07 says the dwelling below is made 'by our deeds throughout the exile' (Tanya 37:1). This cluster is that clause opened out. Exile is the soul's and the Shechinah's descent into real concealment.

family: 197 subjects in 16 clusters, each shown as a face of the one idea
title: K16 · The Physical: Body, Food, Money and Nature
abstract: These twelve subjects are the one idea at its lowest point, where the spine says it shows most fully (Inyanah 19:4; Tanya 36). Each is read the same way. First, the thing exists and lives now by the word of God within it: food, stone, body (F01; SH 1:4-5, 2:5; Keter Shem Tov 1:159); livelihood comes down as creation from nothing, its substance from the inwardness of Ein Sof (the Rashab, Umaayan 22, 24). Second, its apparent independence is a concealment.

title: Unity Index · Works · group-01
abstract: What it is. Unedited transcripts ('hanachas hatmimim bilti mugah') of the Rebbe's farbrengens, mostly Yiddish, with Hebrew reworkings in the later volumes. Forty-six scanned volumes. The file's volume labels are OCR-derived and often wrong: e.g. the block labelled תש"ו opens 'ה'תש"ל חלק ב'', and the one labelled תש"י opens 'ה'תשל"ה חלק א''. title: Unity Index · Works · group-02
abstract: What it is. The Rebbe's talks (sichos) and discourses (maamarim) in the edited Hebrew 'Toras Menachem – Hisvaaduyos' series. Despite the '1950-1992' in the file name, the file holds 73 volumes running from 14 Shevat 5710 (the week after the Rayatz's passing, line 1) to the Rosh Hashanah telegram of 5733-34 (the last line). From volume נא (5728, line 100948) the lines become long paragraphs (about 400-500 lines per volume instead of 2,000+), so line counts from 5728 on are not comparable with the earlier volumes.

title: Unity Index · Works · group-03
abstract: Group summary. Group-03 spans the whole map. Two Chabad works carry the idea as their stated center: Likkutei Sichos proves it on Rashi and the Rambam and maps the two unities onto two Torah genres, and Kuntres HaTefillah brings it from knowledge into prayer. Likkutei Biurim (badly OCR'd) turns bitul inward against spiritual ecstasy.

family: 220 works, each read for how it carries the unity
title: Unity Index · Works · group-04
abstract: Group-04 is uneven, and its spread is its lesson. The Rebbeim's own texts state the idea, each from its side. The Rebbe's letters use ein od as an answer to scientists, mystics and people in trouble, and turn particular providence into the hinge of the practical letter. Toras Chaim works the Mitteler Rebbe's detail-to-Essence method at maamar length, with the two unities as its frame and their future equality below. Kuntres HaHitpa'alut tests whether contemplated Godliness has reached the heart, and roots that knowing in the yechidah.

family: 220 works, each read for how it carries the unity
title: Unity Index · Works · group-05
abstract: Group-05 has twenty-two works: thirteen from the Chabad Rebbeim and the Strashelye circle, nine from other schools. The Chabad maamar collections carry the one idea as their stated center, each from its own side. Torah Ohr and Likkutei Torah take it through the year of Torah readings. Torah Ohr gives the spine's own 'yachid, not echad' in the Alter Rebbe's words (Megillat Esther, 2378). Likkutei Torah has the most material on the two unities and on 'know today'.

Tzadok of Lublin, Polonne, Ujhel, the Besht anthology, Ruzhin, Ger). The Chabad maamar collections carry the one idea as their stated center, each from its own side. The Rebbe's Sefer HaMaamarim Melukat has the most 'Essence' and 'dwelling below' in the group.

title: Unity Index · Works · group-07
abstract: Group-07 has twenty-five works: twelve by the Chabad Rebbeim, six modern histories and compilations from the Agudas Chassidei Chabad library, and seven from other schools. The idea is stated as the book's own subject in all four of the Mitteler Rebbe's works here. Imrei Binah opens by saying that all the Alter Rebbe's teaching was 'to fix the simple unity of God, the Essence of Ein Sof, in the mind and heart of each one', and it makes 'know today' a duty of knowledge, not faith alone.

family: 220 works, each read for how it carries the unity
title: Unity Index · Works · group-08
abstract: Group-08 has thirty-two works: twenty-two flagged Chabad in the index and ten not. The index's non-Chabad flag includes the Alter Rebbe's Hilkhot Talmud Torah and Strashelye's Sha'arei Avodah. In the Chabad core the one idea is the stated center, and each work shows a different side of it. Tanya makes it the inheritance of every Jew (ch. 33, 36) and grounds creation in the Essence (IH 20). The Alter Rebbe's late maamarim state 'yachid, not echad' and require both knowledges 'below as above' through mitzvot.

title: Unity Index · Works · group-10
abstract: Group-10 has fourteen works: seven Chabad and seven not. In the Chabad maamarim the one idea is the stated center, and each work gives it a different angle. The Alter Rebbe's Maamarei Admur HaZaken states the dwelling below as the purpose of all worlds, a will whose reason is unknown. Its content is turning darkness to light, and it defines a dwelling as what is batel to the one who dwells in it (F07 = F08).

family: 220 works, each read for how it carries the unity
title: Unity Index · Works · group-11
abstract: Group-11 has twelve works: seven Chabad (the Rebbe's Inyanah; three by the Tzemach Tzedek; the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch; the Rashab's Ayin Beis; the Maharash's Toras Shmuel) and five from other schools (Breslov, Arvei Nachal, Ropshitz, Lizhensk, Hillel Zeitlin). Inyanah Shel Toras HaChassidus is the thesis itself. It says Chassidus is one point, the drawing down of Ein Sof, 'the essential', and that 'ein od milvado' means the worlds as they are, in time and space, are united with the Essence, not that they vanish.

family: 220 works, each read for how it carries the unity
title: Unity Index · Works · group-12
abstract: Summary. Group-12 has seven works: one Chabad and six from other schools. The one idea is present in all seven, but each carries it differently, and the group shows clearly where it is the organizing center and where it is only the ground. The Tzemach Tzedek's Or HaTorah (6.75M words, OCR, with three garbled Rashi-script blocks) works the idea verse by verse through Torah, Nach, Siddur and Chazal.

family: The meditation behind every face and every subject
title: The meditation behind each face
abstract: Every concept in Chassidus points to one thing, the unity of God, and that unity cannot be understood: by definition it is beyond the mind. The Tanya says so and also says what to do about it. Knowing, da'at, is binding the mind to a truth until it is as real as a thing seen with the eyes; without that binding, even a wise understanding breeds only imaginings (Likkutei Amarim 3 and 42). Where the mind ends, faith carries on.

family: One process: knowing the unity is meditating on it
title: One process: knowing the unity is meditating on it
abstract: In Chassidus, to know that there is nothing but Him is already to meditate on it: knowing (da'at) means holding a truth until it is real, so each rung of the unity is known only by a matching depth of contemplation and of self-giving (bitul), and each one wakes a deeper layer of the soul, until at the bottom of the self, where the mind stops, the heart's simple will is already one with Him; and from there it comes back down, into the body and the day.

family: The Tanya, line by line
title: The Tanya, line by line: one idea
abstract: The Tanya is not five books on five subjects. It is one idea said again and again, from every side: there is nothing but God, and the world, the soul, the struggle and the deed are how that truth becomes real down here. So more than half the book says it in so many words, and more than eight lines in ten either say it or build toward it. Nothing was forced: where a line has no tie, it is marked "none".

family: The Tanya, line by line
title: Tanya, lines 1-280: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: This is not the part of Tanya where the unity is taught directly. That happens in chapters 20-25 and 33-37 and in Shaar HaYichud VehaEmunah. Chapters 1-18 are anthropology and method. They describe the two souls, the soul's faculties and garments, kelipah and nogah, the five types of person, and the beinoni. The unity comes in at a few points and carries weight there. Most lines are structural, meaning they are definitions and steps the later chapters need. The dominant faces follow from that.

family: The Tanya, line by line
title: Tanya, lines 281-560: Likkutei Amarim 18:11 to 38:15
abstract: Faces carried by the whole-line entries: F10 Torah/mitzvah 62 · F07 home below 47 · F11 darkness to light 47 · F08 bitul 46 · F06 soul 45 · F03 hiding 34 · F02 two unities 31 · F12 knowing 28 · F05 Essence 19 · F01 speech now 11 · F04 filling/surrounding 9 · F09 opposites 9.

family: The Tanya, line by line
title: Tanya, lines 561-840: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: The earlier range (lines 1-280) was mostly anthropology, and there the unity came in only at a few points. This range is the reverse. Much of it teaches the unity outright. Chapters 41-53 turn the soul's love and awe into contemplation of Ein Sof. Chapter 48 defines sovev and memale. Chapters 49 and 53 name the purpose of all tzimtzumim and of all worlds. Shaar HaYichud 1-7 then sets out the core doctrine of F01, F02 and F03 step by step. That is why stated dominates.

family: The Mitteler Rebbe's Gate of Unity, line by line
title: The Gate of Unity, line by line: one idea in every detail
abstract: The Tanya says the one idea from every side. The Gate of Unity walks it down, one rung at a time. The book names its own subject in its first line: "the unity of Godliness in every single detail" of the chain of worlds. Then it keeps that promise: every rung, from God's first will down to the last blade of grass, is one with its source; the end is fixed in the beginning; and the work of a person is to know this detail by detail until it lives …

family: The Mitteler Rebbe's Gate of Unity, line by line
title: The Gate of Unity, lines 1-905: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: The book names its own subject in its first line: "the unity of Godliness in every single detail" of the chain of worlds (line 1). The rest of the range keeps to that. It has three parts. Chapters 1-6 (8-286) are about how to know. They set out what contemplation is (Binah, Tevunah, Da'at). They say it must go detail by detail and be joined to the whole. They say it must produce two opposite feelings together, joy and bitul. Most lines are structural definitions of the mind.

family: The Mitteler Rebbe's Gate of Unity, line by line
title: The Gate of Unity, lines 906-1810: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: This range is the reverse of the Tanya range 561-840. There, stated made up two thirds of the entries. Here it is about one line in six. These seventeen chapters are the Mitteler Rebbe's walk through the chain of worlds: the primordial will, the kav and the circles, Adam Kadmon, tohu and tikkun, the three lines, Atik and Arich, Abba and Imma, lights and vessels, and the start of Zeir Anpin. Most lines are steps in that mechanism.

family: The Mitteler Rebbe's Gate of Unity, line by line
title: The Gate of Unity, lines 1811-2713: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: This is the second half of a book whose introduction says what it is about: "the unity of Godliness in every single detail" of the chain of worlds. The range does exactly that, and so most of it is mapping. Line after line places one partzuf, one letter or one Name inside the next. That is why structural dominates (84% of lines), and why most structural lines carry no face. The Tanya's Shaar HaYichud states the unity in seven short chapters.

family: Imrei Binah: the Shema as the place where the one idea is made
title: Imrei Binah, line by line: the Shema as the place where the one idea is made
abstract: The Gate of Unity walks the unity down the chain of worlds, rung by rung. Imrei Binah takes one verse, "Hear, O Israel, Havayah is our God, Havayah is One", and asks how a person saying it makes the unity happen. The book names its subject in its first lines. The Alter Rebbe's whole teaching, the author says, was to fix "the simple unity of God, which is the Essence of the Infinite", in the mind and heart of every Jew (line 3).

family: Imrei Binah: the Shema as the place where the one idea is made
title: Imrei Binah, lines 1-98: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: This range is almost all doctrine, and the text itself says it is about the unity. The introduction names the book's subject: the Alter Rebbe taught only to fix "the simple unity" in mind and heart, and this book is on the higher and lower unity of the Shema. Petach HaShaar then works through one verse, the first verse of the Shema, from every side.

family: Imrei Binah: the Shema as the place where the one idea is made
title: Imrei Binah, lines 99-181: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: This is the heart of the book's commentary on the first verse of the Shema. The range asks one question in many forms: how can the One who is alone (yachid) also be the One of all things (echad), with no change between them? §3-5 (99-110): the body as a map. The heart, the lungs, the stomach and the diaphragm are read as a map of Atzilut. The "firmament" that divides the upper from the lower waters is the organ that separates the fine from the coarse.

family: Imrei Binah: the Shema as the place where the one idea is made
title: Imrei Binah, lines 182-265: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: This part of the book is a commentary on the Shema, and it has one question at its centre. Why does the lower unity (Baruch Shem, God's kingship in time and space) have an advantage over the higher unity of the first verse (line 183)? The Gate of Unity already set the two unities side by side. This range argues that the lower one reaches higher.

family: Imrei Binah: the Shema as the place where the one idea is made
title: Imrei Binah, lines 266-351: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: The range is one long commentary on the Shema, read word by word, from "Shema Yisrael" to "va'ed". It has four parts. Sections 45-49 (266-281): the first verse and Baruch Shem. The souls' self-sacrifice in "Shema Yisrael" raises the fallen sparks up to the Essence. From there a new light comes down into Chochmah and Binah ("Havayah Elokeinu"). "Havayah echad" then unites the divided attributes, and Baruch Shem is the lower unity in time. F05, F02 and F09 lead here. Sections 49-53 (278-296): the two paragraphs.

family: Imrei Binah: the Shema as the place where the one idea is made
title: Imrei Binah, lines 352-437: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: The range continues the word-by-word reading of the Shema. It has three movements. Sections 70-83 (352-401): the letters of "echad" and "va'ed", and what they spell. "Va'ed" is "echad" with letters exchanged: the higher unity carried into the lower. The aleph becomes a vav, a hidden line of the surrounding light that is equal in every world. The chet becomes an ayin, the outside of Chochmah. The dalet stays a dalet.

family: Imrei Binah: the Shema as the place where the one idea is made
title: Imrei Binah, lines 438-521: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: This range is not like the Gate of Unity ranges, where the rungs of the worlds are mostly structural and the tie comes up every twenty or thirty lines. Here the long paragraphs are arguments about practice: Torah study against the deed, tzitzit, joy and fear, teshuvah. Almost every column reaches its tie before it ends. So stated dominates the line entries (68 of 84). The honest count is really the sub-entries: about two in three of them are stated.

family: Imrei Binah: the Shema as the place where the one idea is made
title: Imrei Binah, lines 522-603: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: The whole range is built on one image: the seal. "Set me as a seal upon Your heart, as a seal upon Your arm" (Song 8:6). A raised seal makes sunken letters in the wax, and a sunken seal makes raised ones. The Mitteler Rebbe uses this to ask one question many times: when a person reaches up, what comes down, and in what form? His answer has two halves. Love and excitement from below, the "running" (ratzo), are a "something".

family: Kuntres HaHitpa'alut: the real arousal and its counterfeits
title: Kuntres HaHitpa'alut, line by line: the real arousal and its counterfeits
abstract: The other books in this index teach the unity. This one teaches how to tell whether it has reached you. It is a field guide to arousal (hitpa'alut) in prayer: what the real thing is, what it is mistaken for, and the signs that tell them apart. Its rule is one sentence. The Alter Rebbe's whole aim was that the chassidim's arousal be "only Godly arousal, and not the arousal of the life of flesh" (line 135). Everything else unpacks the word "Godly".

family: Kuntres HaHitpa'alut: the real arousal and its counterfeits
title: Kuntres HaHitpa'alut, lines 1-912: the real arousal and its counterfeits
abstract: This book does not teach the unity. It teaches how to tell whether the unity has reached you. It is a field guide to arousal (hitpa'alut): what the real thing is, what it is mistaken for, and how to tell them apart. So the faces that lead are the three faces of the person's side: - F08: bitul, the absence of self-feeling. - F12: knowing that moves from mind into heart. - F06: the soul as a part of God.

family: The Rebbe Rashab on prayer: Kuntres HaTefillah and Kuntres HaAvodah
title: Kuntres HaTefillah, line by line: prayer as the place where knowing the unity becomes real
abstract: This is not a book about the unity. It is a book about how knowing the unity is made real in a person, and prayer is where that happens. Study, the Rashab says, is only the preparation (line 49). The main thing is the verse "know today and return it to your heart", and the main word in it is the heart (line 62).

family: The Rebbe Rashab on prayer: Kuntres HaTefillah and Kuntres HaAvodah
title: Kuntres HaAvodah, line by line: prayer as the place where the unity is felt
abstract: This is not a book about the unity of God. It is a book about how a person at prayer comes to feel what the Tanya and its Gate of Unity teach. Its heading gives the verse it lives by: the service of the heart is to bind the soul to Godliness and refine the animal soul, "as it says, know today and return it to your heart" (lines 23-25).

family: The Rebbe Rashab on prayer: Kuntres HaTefillah and Kuntres HaAvodah
title: Kuntres HaTefillah, lines 1-253: prayer as the place where knowing the unity becomes real
abstract: This is not a book about the unity. It is a book about how knowing the unity is made real in a person, and prayer is where that happens. That is why F12 ("know today and return it to your heart") runs through almost every line. It is also why so many lines are structural: they build the psychology the F12 teaching needs (Da'at as feeling, mind drawing the heart, "surrounding" against "inner" light, the vessel).

family: The Rebbe Rashab on prayer: Kuntres HaTefillah and Kuntres HaAvodah
title: Kuntres HaAvodah, lines 1-306: prayer as the place where the unity is known
abstract: This is a book about practice, not about cosmology. Its question is how a person at prayer comes to feel what the Tanya and Shaar HaYichud teach. So F12 (knowing the unity until the heart is moved) leads by a wide margin. F11 (refining the animal soul) comes next, because refining the animal soul is one of the two named aims of prayer. F08 (bitul) and F06 (the soul as part of God) follow. The cosmological faces F01-F05 appear mostly as the content of contemplation.

family: Hemshech Samach Vav: the Essence below, through the will that has no reason
title: Hemshech Samach Vav, line by line: the Essence below, through the will that has no reason
abstract: The Tanya asks how the world can be, if there is nothing but God. The Gate of Unity walks the unity down the chain of worlds. Imrei Binah asks how saying the Shema makes it. Samach Vav asks a sharper question than any of them, and asks it in its first maamar: why are there worlds at all?

family: Hemshech Samach Vav: the Essence below, through the will that has no reason
title: Hemshech Samach Vav, lines 1-759: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: This is the opening of the great 5666 series, and it is organized around one question: why are there worlds at all? The answer is stated in the first maamar and never dropped: So the leading faces are F05 (the Essence) and F10 (Torah and mitzvot), not the cosmological F01-F02 that lead in the Tanya's Shaar HaYichud. The Rashab's unity is not first "the world is nullified in its source". It is "the Essence, which no light reaches, is drawn below through the mitzvah".

family: Hemshech Samach Vav: the Essence below, through the will that has no reason
title: Hemshech Samach Vav, lines 760-1421: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: The range covers the maamarim for the Shabbatot of Noach to Vayishlach 5666 (autumn 1905): the end of the opening of Eleh Toldos Noach (760-864), Vayomer... Lech Lecha (865-979), Ki Yedativ (980-1086), Ve'Avraham Zaken (1087-1156), Vayiten Lecha (1157-1282), Vayetze (1283-1401) and the first page of Vayishlach (1402-1421). The Tanya shows the unity mostly as creation and nullification (F01, F02, F03). This range works on a different axis.

family: Hemshech Samach Vav: the Essence below, through the will that has no reason
title: Hemshech Samach Vav, lines 1422-2062: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: The first range (lines 1-759) asked why there are worlds at all. This range asks how a person reaches the Essence, and what reaches it. The answer runs through all six maamarim. Light, even the highest light, runs back to its source. Only the Essence, which has no source to run to, can come down and stay. So the person who most truly reaches the Essence is the one who comes back down: into Torah and mitzvot, into the animal soul, into eating and business.

family: Hemshech Samach Vav: the Essence below, through the will that has no reason
title: Hemshech Samach Vav, lines 2063-2700: what "Ein Sof" names, and why the world is "from nothing"
abstract: The range starts partway through HaChodesh HaZeh Lachem (Shabbat Bo, 8 Shevat 5666) and runs to the first page of Kedoshim Tihyu (Shabbat Acharei-Kedoshim, 10 Iyar). The maamarim are: These maamarim form one argument. Each Shabbat's verse is used to take the argument a step further, and the step it takes is metaphysical. The range asks: - What does the word "Ein Sof" actually name? - Why is creation called "from nothing" (yesh me'ayin) when "everything is from You"? - How can the infinite be limited at all?

family: Hemshech Samach Vav: the Essence below, through the will that has no reason
title: Hemshech Samach Vav, lines 2701-3377: Havayah and Elokim, the two knowledges, and the far surrounding
abstract: Lines 1422-2062 asked how a person reaches the Essence. This range asks what stands between a person and the Essence, and whether it truly stands between. Its answer is built on two Names. Havayah is the source of all being. Elokim is the "shield and sheath" that hides Havayah so that a separate world can exist. The range then asks what the hiding really is, and gives three answers that deepen one another:

family: Hemshech Samach Vav: the Essence below, through the will that has no reason
title: Hemshech Samach Vav, lines 3378-3942: the Essence reached by "no", the will that is everywhere, and prayer "from behind"
abstract: The range opens in the middle of Nasso Es Rosh (Shabbat Nasso, 9 Sivan 5666) and runs into the middle of UMikneh Rav (Shabbat Matos-Masei, Mevarchim Menachem-Av). The maamarim are: The previous ranges were metaphysics: what "Ein Sof" names and why the world is "from nothing". This range turns that metaphysics into service. It asks three questions: - What does each kind of commandment reach in God?

family: Hemshech Samach Vav: the Essence below, through the will that has no reason
title: Hemshech Samach Vav, lines 3943-4518: the simple servant, the end wedged in the beginning, and the nothing of Keter
abstract: The range starts at the last page of UMikneh Rav (Matos-Masei 5666) and runs through the High Holiday and Sukkos maamarim of 5667, stopping in the middle of BaYom HaShemini Atzeres. The range is one long argument in three stages. 1. The servants (3948-4088). There are three ways to serve: the son, the trusted servant (who serves from love) and the simple servant (who serves only under the yoke). The simple servant, the lowest, reaches highest.

family: Hemshech Samach Vav: the Essence below, through the will that has no reason
title: Hemshech Samach Vav, lines 4519-5139: the white that adds nothing, Torah that joins two essences, and the yoke that reaches the Essence
abstract: The range opens in the middle of Bayom HaShmini Atzeres and ends at the start of Kol HaShoneh Halachos. The maamarim are: Between 4899 and 4900 the dates jump from Marcheshvan to Iyar. The maamarim between them are not in this file. Across all seven maamarim there is really one argument, told from several sides. It goes like this: - Light is not a thing next to the Essence. It is the Essence revealed, and that is why it can unite with everything.

family: Hemshech Samach Vav: the Essence below, through the will that has no reason
title: Hemshech Samach Vav, lines 5140-5774: truth to its truth, the Name with no meaning, and the engraved letter
abstract: The range starts in the middle of Kol HaShoneh Halachos (Emor 5667) and ends in the middle of Ein Omdin Lehispallel (Naso 5667). It covers the maamarim from Lag BaOmer season through Shavuos. The editor notes (5347) that BeShaah SheHikdimu and the seven maamarim after it form a unit within the Hemshech, and (5334) that Im Bechukosai closes an argument begun at the very start of the Hemshech. The range runs in three movements. 1. Truth to its truth (5140-5339).

family: Hemshech Samach Vav: the Essence below, through the will that has no reason
title: Hemshech Samach Vav, lines 5775-6399: the soul's root in the Essence, the ascent through descent, and the mitzvah that reaches what Torah reveals
abstract: The five maamarim of winter 5668 are really one argument in five steps. That is why F05 (the Essence) and F06 (the soul) dominate the counts here, with F10 (Torah and mitzvah) third. 1. The soul's root is in "letters engraved right through". Those letters are no being of their own. They are one with the light of Ein Sof before the tzimtzum, "He and His Name are one". 2. The soul came down into the lowest body "with force", from the Essence.

family: Hemshech Samach Vav: the Essence below, through the will that has no reason
title: Hemshech Samach Vav, lines 6400-7270: the Essence on Yom Kippur, the notes of the Rayatz, and the Rebbe's summary of the series
abstract: The range has three parts that speak about the unity, with a dead zone in the middle. The end of the series (6400-6497). The Rashab wrote this conclusion but did not deliver it. It ranks three levels. Malchiyos and Zichronos draw the filling and surrounding light as they are rooted before the tzimtzum. Shofros draws the Essence itself, above both. Rosh Hashanah begins that drawing and Yom Kippur completes it. The appendices of the Rayatz and the Rebbe (6498-6711). The Rayatz's notes are mostly about the grades of love.

family: Hemshech Samach Vav: the Essence below, through the will that has no reason
title: Hemshech Samach Vav, lines 7271-8119: the editor's summaries of the series, and the start of the subject index
abstract: Because the editor boils each discourse down to its conclusion, this range is the densest statement of the series' thesis anywhere in the book. The thesis comes through the same way in both the chapter-heads and the summary. The world, the light, even Ein Sof as the Kabbalists name it, are all "name and glimmer". What God wants is not that glimmer made bright.

family: Hemshech Samach Vav: the Essence below, through the will that has no reason
title: Hemshech Samach Vav, lines 8120-9229: the indexes at the back of the book
abstract: Almost all of the content is in the first 388 lines. The subject index from מ to ת happens to cover most of the series' key terms: מלכות, ממלא and סובב, מצות, נשמות, נתאוה (the dwelling below), עבד, עצמות, צמצום, קו, רצון, רצוא ושוב, תורה, תשובה. Read in a row, the glosses give a compressed map of the whole series. F05 (the Essence) leads by far, as in the rest of the book. F10 (Torah and mitzvot) is second.

family: Hemshech Ayin Beis: the Essence that hides in order to shine
title: Hemshech Ayin Beis, line by line: the Essence that hides in order to shine, and the one who knows it
abstract: Samach Vav asks why there are worlds at all. Ayin Beis asks the next question, and keeps asking it for four years: how does anything come from the Essence and still show it? How does light come from what is not light, many from what is simple, a "something" from what is no thing? Its answer turns the usual picture of hiding around. The hiding is not the price of revelation. It is how revelation happens.

family: Hemshech Ayin Beis: the Essence that hides in order to shine
title: Hemshech Ayin Beis, lines 1-587: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: Samach Vav asks why there are worlds at all. Ayin Beis asks something narrower: how, exactly, does light come from the Essence? The Rashab takes nothing about "light" for granted. The first 78 chapters are one long analysis of inner light (or pnimi) and surrounding light (or makif). He looks at their roots before the tzimtzum, at the lights and the vessels of Atzilut, at the ten sefirot hidden in Ein Sof, at the will, and at the Essence above even the will.

family: Hemshech Ayin Beis: the Essence that hides in order to shine
title: Hemshech Ayin Beis, lines 588-1167: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: Hemshech Ayin Beis is one long series of discourses, not a set of separate maamarim. Each Shabbat or festival adds chapters to a single argument. In this range the argument is about the word sefirah. The Rashab reads it four ways: as number (mispar), as telling (sippur), as sapphire brightness (sapir), and as a book or parchment (sefer). Each reading answers one question: how does anything limited (a sefirah, a vessel, a world) come from the Ein Sof, and how does it still show the Ein Sof?

family: Hemshech Ayin Beis: the Essence that hides in order to shine
title: Hemshech Ayin Beis, lines 1168-1742: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: The earlier ranges of this series asked how the limited comes from Ein Sof and still shows it. This range asks how anything connects to the Essence (atzmus) itself. The theme appears in many forms: the "intermediary" (memutza) between Ein Sof and the worlds: the line, Atzilut, Adam Kadmon, and finally Keter and hidden Chochmah; - the two unions "He and His life" and "He and His bones"; - the three knots: the Holy One, Torah and Israel; - will and delight; - the surround that is hidden only from …

family: Hemshech Ayin Beis: the Essence that hides in order to shine
title: Hemshech Ayin Beis, lines 1743-2315: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: These seventeen maamarim are one argument. It asks what makes the difference between Tohu and Tikkun, and how opposites can become one. The answer the Rashab builds step by step is bitul, and the root of bitul is the Essence. That is why F05 (the Essence) and F08 (bitul) lead the count by a wide margin. F12 (knowing) comes third, because the second half of the range is a long study of how knowledge works: hearing and seeing, comprehension and sight, speech and the face.

family: Hemshech Ayin Beis: the Essence that hides in order to shine
title: Hemshech Ayin Beis, lines 2316-2881: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: This range is sixteen maamarim, from the summer of 1914 into the autumn. They pursue one question: how can the Essence, which is simple and one, be the source of a world that is many, separate and "yesh"? The previous range (1743-2315) asked how opposites become one, and answered: through bitul. This range turns to the other side, the coming-into-being of the "yesh" itself. That is why F01 (the world said into being now) and F03 (the hiding) rise sharply here, next to F05 (the Essence) and F08 (bitul).

family: Hemshech Ayin Beis: the Essence that hides in order to shine
title: Hemshech Ayin Beis, lines 2882-3429: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: These are the Shabbat maamarim of the winter of 1914-15, from Lech Lecha to Mishpatim. The previous range asked how the simple Essence can be the source of a world that is many and "yesh". This range turns to how the Essence is drawn down and revealed, and what in the person and in Torah can receive it. Two contrasts run through it: the Written Torah and prayer, and drawing from above and ascent from below. F05 (the Essence) leads the count.

family: Hemshech Ayin Beis: the Essence that hides in order to shine
title: Hemshech Ayin Beis, lines 3430-3941: the tzimtzum that does not reach the Essence, and the tzimtzum turned to light
abstract: Seventeen maamarim, from Shekalim to Shavuot 1915. The previous ranges asked how the simple One becomes a world of many and of "yesh". This range asks the next question: after the tzimtzum and all the screens, how can the Essence of Ein Sof be revealed here below, without the world being wiped out? That is why F03 (the hiding) is second only to F05 (the Essence). The answer is built in six stages:

family: Hemshech Ayin Beis: the Essence that hides in order to shine
title: Hemshech Ayin Beis, lines 3942-4471: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: This is one long argument carried across nineteen maamarim, week by week through the summer of 1915. The Rashab picks up each week exactly where he stopped ("ולהבין זה ילה"ק משנת"ל", "to understand this, first recall what was explained"). The thread is how the Essence comes to be in the lower world, and what in the person and the world is the vessel for it. The key words move in order: vessel and light, running and returning, refinement, delight, rest, gift, and at the end yesh and ayin.

family: Hemshech Ayin Beis: the Essence that hides in order to shine
title: Hemshech Ayin Beis, lines 4472-5017: the two knowledges, the vessel turned to light, and the concealment that will shine
abstract: These maamarim have one thread, stated at the start: there are three levels, "yesh, ayin, yesh". The first yesh is the true Yesh, the Essence. The second is the created yesh. Between them is the ayin, and the ayin itself divides in two. From that the Rashab builds the two knowledges. The higher knowledge (da'at elyon) is the giver's view: "above is yesh, below is ayin". The lower knowledge (da'at tachton) is the receiver's view: "below is yesh, above is ayin".

family: Hemshech Ayin Beis: the Essence that hides in order to shine
title: Hemshech Ayin Beis, lines 5018-5750: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: The written continuation began (line 4683) by asking what "there is nothing else" (אין עוד) adds to "Havayah is Elokim". This range is its long second half, and it ends by answering that question. The Rashab moves by chains of verses and parables. The paragraphs are long, some run past 1,800 characters, and many parts end with a gloss that opens a new question. The thread is how darkness, the yesh and the lower worlds are joined to the Essence.

family: R. Aharon of Strashelye's Sha'arei HaYichud VeEmunah
title: Sha'arei HaYichud VeEmunah, line by line: one idea
abstract: The Tanya comes back to the unity from many subjects. This book has no other subject. The author says he is explaining "root premises" he received from the Alter Rebbe, who set them out "a little" in the Tanya's Gate of Unity and Faith. So the whole book is one idea, taken through the whole of Kabbalah: God is alone after creation just as He was before, and every level, screen and name in the Kabbalah is how He looks from our side.

family: R. Aharon of Strashelye's Sha'arei HaYichud VeEmunah
title: Sha'arei HaYichud VeEmunah, lines 1-96: the Preface and the Introduction
abstract: The Preface is a defence of writing the book. It is not yet the doctrine. Still, it keeps stopping to say what the doctrine is for. So F12 (knowing the unity, and bringing that knowing to the heart) runs through the whole Preface. It leads the count, as in no Tanya range. The Preface also shows the author's method. It sets three conditions on explaining by parable (lines 33-50).

family: R. Aharon of Strashelye's Sha'arei HaYichud VeEmunah
title: Sha'arei HaYichud VeEmunah, lines 97-281: the First Gate, "the gate of the whole of the unity"
abstract: This gate is not a book that sometimes reaches the unity. The unity is its only subject. The author, R. Aharon HaLevi of Strashelye, a leading student of the Alter Rebbe, says he is explaining "root premises received from the light of our holy Rebbe's Torah", which the Rebbe set out "a little in his holy book, in Shaar HaYichud VehaEmunah" (line 98). So nearly every line is stated.

family: R. Aharon of Strashelye's Sha'arei HaYichud VeEmunah
title: Sha'arei HaYichud VeEmunah, lines 282-421: the first half of the Second Gate
abstract: The gate asks one technical question: why the sefirot are exactly ten, "ten and not nine, ten and not eleven" (line 282). Answering it takes the author through the whole structure of the worlds. At each step he stops to say that the structure is ours, not His. Lines 282-309 build an anatomy of every created thing. Each has reason (mushkal), nature (mutba) and felt body (murgash). Each of these has three lines, which makes nine, and the form that shows them is the tenth.

family: R. Aharon of Strashelye's Sha'arei HaYichud VeEmunah
title: Sha'arei HaYichud VeEmunah, lines 422-562: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: The whole range is one argument, and it is almost all stated. That is why so few lines are structural and only one is none. R. Aharon keeps asking one question: how can God be described at all? His answer runs through every chapter. There are two sides, "relative to us" (לגבי דידן) and "relative to Him" (לגביה). Whatever divides, hides, contracts or is "known" is on our side. With Him "all is in total equality" (בהשואה גמורה).

family: R. Aharon of Strashelye's Sha'arei HaYichud VeEmunah
title: Sha'arei HaYichud VeEmunah, lines 563-778: the Third Gate, the gate of the "faces"
abstract: The Third Gate is one long argument, and nearly all of it is about the unity. Its tools are the Zohar's Idra Rabba and Idra Zuta and the Etz Chayim: Arich Anpin and Zeir Anpin, and the skull, brain, hair, eyes, nose, forehead, mouth and beard of each. The argument does not use them as a map of the upper worlds for its own sake.

family: R. Aharon of Strashelye's Sha'arei HaYichud VeEmunah
title: Sha'arei HaYichud VeEmunah, lines 779-931: the Fourth Gate, the Gate of Lights and Vessels
abstract: The gate is a single long argument about one question. How can the infinite show itself in something finite without either one cancelling the other? Its tools are the Lurianic terms: kav (the line), igul (the circle), reshimu (the trace), Adam Kadmon, shevirah and tikkun (breaking and repair), parsa (the screen), and heichalot (palaces). But the author keeps turning every term back to one claim. All the grades, screens and differences exist only "toward us". Toward Him, "all is one":

family: R. Aharon of Strashelye's Sha'arei HaYichud VeEmunah
title: Sha'arei HaYichud VeEmunah, lines 932-1093: the Fifth Gate, katnut and gadlut
abstract: The gate is called "the Gate of Katnut and Gadlut" (smallness and growth). On its surface it is a guide to the Lurianic partzufim: Arich Anpin, Abba and Imma, Yisrael Saba and Tevunah, Ze'ir Anpin and Nukva. It covers their gestation, nursing and growth, their outer and inner vessels, and the joint-by-joint maps of Etz Chaim. About a third of the lines are that mapping, and they are marked structural.

family: Sefer HaArachim Chabad, volume 9: the entries on the unity
title: Sefer HaArachim Chabad vol. 9, Achdus Hashem: lines 2051-4101
abstract: The heart of the range is Achdus Hashem (6), the higher and the lower unity: 23 sections that set out the doctrine carefully and in layers. Its main lessons for the index: - Continuous creation, the SPINE's F01, is only the lower unity. It is the first rung, not the summit (line 2276). - The unity has three rungs, lower unity, higher unity and Yachid. The SPINE's "yachid" is above even the higher unity (lines 2999, 3912).

family: Sefer HaArachim Chabad, volume 9: the entries on the unity
title: Sefer HaArachim Chabad, vol. 9: the unity entries, lines 1-2050
abstract: The volume's thesis is the paradox itself (T1). Nothing exists besides Him, and the world is really created. Chassidus holds that the two reinforce each other, and it grounds the world's reality in Torah, the mitzvos and the dwelling below. The SPINE's "yachid, not echad" needs rewording (§3). "Havayah echad (not yachid)" is deliberate, and echad in its deepest sense means the world's existence is itself united with Him (T5). The highest unity is not the world's negation but its union with the Essence, which bears opposites (T9).

family: Darkei HaChassidus: how the unity becomes a life
title: Darkei HaChassidus: how the unity becomes a life
abstract: Chassidus is not only the idea that there is nothing but G-d. It is also a way of making that idea into the person, and the sources call that way the whole point: «כל ענין החסידות הוא לשנות טבע מדותיו» (The whole point of Chassidus is to change the nature of one's traits. The Rebbe, Inyanah Shel Toras HaChassidus §1, line 7). The way is a daily loop. The night before, you prepare.

family: Darkei HaChassidus: how the unity becomes a life
title: Darkei HaChassidus, sources A: the Alter Rebbe and the Rebbe Rashab (with R. Hillel of Paritch and R. Aharon of Strashelye)
abstract: Where the OCR has an obvious slip, the Hebrew is left as the scan has it and the intended word follows in square brackets, e.g. "חפידות [חסידות]". The bracketed words are ours and are not part of the verified string. Abbreviations the scans use: דא"ח (Chassidus), אהוי"ר (love and fear), נה"ב / נה"א (the animal soul / the Divine soul), עומ"ש / קבעומ"ש (the yoke of heaven), מחדו"מ (thought, speech, deed), טו"ד (reason and understanding).

family: Darkei HaChassidus: how the unity becomes a life
title: Darkei HaChassidus, sources D: the wider Chassidic world beyond Chabad
abstract: Each school carries the same idea (G-d fills and enlivens everything; the self is to become transparent to Him) into life by a different main door. In one line each, with the item numbers below that support it:

family: Darkei HaChassidus: how the unity becomes a life
title: Darkei HaChassidus: sources B (the Lubavitcher Rebbe, the Tzemach Tzedek, the Maharash, R. Yitzchak Eizik of Homel, and the Rebbe Rayatz items gathered before the scope change)
abstract: What this file is. The raw material for darkei haChassidus, the Chassidic way of life that carries the idea (the unity, SPINE.md, ONE-PROCESS.md) into the whole person and the whole day. It collects what these sources say about integration: how an understood truth becomes the person. It is organised under the five headings of the brief. Scope.

family: Darkei HaChassidus: how the unity becomes a life
title: Darkei HaChassidus: sources C, the Rebbe Rayatz
abstract: What the Frierdiker Rebbe (R. Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, 1880-1950) says about how the idea becomes a life: what a Chassid is, avodah and "working on oneself", hisbonenus and davening, learning Chassidus, the farbrengen, the mashpia and the chaver, hiskashrus, ahavas Yisrael, the Chassidic day, and the counterfeits. He tells a great many stories of old Chassidim, and most of them are about exactly this, so they get their own section (1b).

family: The Rambam: one G-d, known by negation, loved by knowing
title: The Rambam: one G-d, known by negation, loved by knowing, served all day
abstract: The Rambam is the one medieval master whom every Chabad Rebbe quotes by name, and argues with by name. His unity has three parts, and each one is a practice as well as a doctrine. He alone truly is. "The foundation of foundations and the pillar of the sciences is to know that there is a First Existent" (mt-01 line 1), and "He alone is the truth, and nothing else has truth like His truth" (mt-01 line 4). All exists "only from the truth of His existence".

family: The Rambam: one G-d, known by negation, loved by knowing
title: Commentary on the Mishnah: the Introduction, Perek Chelek with the Thirteen Principles, and Avot
abstract: The Introduction to the Mishnah (Hakdamah). The Oral Torah given at Sinai with the Written (lines 4-30); how a prophet is tested, and that prophecy decides nothing in the law (lines 31-96); the chain from Moses to Rabbi Judah the Prince (lines 97-116); the kinds of law and the plan of the Mishnah; the worth of the Sages' aggadah, which hides divine matters in riddles (lines 265-306); and then the purpose of creation (lines 307-355). Perek Chelek (Sanhedrin 10).

family: The Rambam: one G-d, known by negation, loved by knowing
title: Mishneh Torah at index level: what each book is and where the inner teaching appears
abstract: The Mishneh Torah has fourteen books (the numerical value of yad, "hand"). The Guide explains the plan (Guide III:35, lines 1223-1238 of guide.txt): each book is a class of commandments with one purpose. Madda holds the beliefs; the rest hold deeds. A pattern runs through the whole work: the Rambam ends many sections of law with a paragraph of inner teaching. Those closing paragraphs are where the guide should look.

family: The Rambam: one G-d, known by negation, loved by knowing
title: Mishneh Torah: the Book of Knowledge, with Prayer, the Mezuzah and the Messiah
abstract: The Mishneh Torah opens with the unity of G-d and not with a law about deeds. The first book, Madda ("Knowledge"), is the Rambam's whole inner path in law form: Yesodei HaTorah (Foundations), 10 chapters. G-d exists, is one, has no body (ch. 1); love and fear, the angels, and His knowing (ch. 2); the heavens and the elements (ch. 3-4), which are "the account of creation"; sanctifying His Name (ch. 5); the holy Names (ch. 6); prophecy and Moses (ch. 7-10). Deot (Dispositions), 7 chapters.

family: The Rambam: one G-d, known by negation, loved by knowing
title: Shemonah Perakim (Eight Chapters): the health of the soul
abstract: Avot is the tractate of chassidut, piety, which "brings to the holy spirit" (line 1). Before explaining it the Rambam gives eight chapters of psychology, drawn from the Sages and the philosophers: "hear the truth from whoever says it" (line 1). The one soul and its five powers (lines 2-11). Which powers hold commandments and sins; virtues of mind and of character (lines 12-13). The sickness of the soul (lines 14-16). The cure: the middle way, and how to return to it (lines 17-30).

family: The Rambam: one G-d, known by negation, loved by knowing
title: The Guide for the Perplexed, Part One: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: Part One is a single long argument that ends in one sentence: G-d is one, and one in a way no word can hold. It gets there in three movements. Clearing the words (chapters 1-49). The Torah says G-d has an image, a face, a back, a place, a throne; that He comes down, goes up, sits, stands, sees, hears. The Rambam walks through each word and shows it has a second, spiritual meaning. "Image" is the mind, not a shape. "Near" is knowing, not place.

family: The Rambam: one G-d, known by negation, loved by knowing
title: The Guide for the Perplexed, Part Three: the chariot, providence, the commandments, and the worship of the one who has understood
abstract: Part Three has five subjects. It climbs from the most hidden (the chariot) to the most practical (how to spend your waking hours). The chariot (III:1-7). A careful, half-veiled reading of Ezekiel's vision. The living creatures "run and return" like lightning, moved by the divine intention. All that is pictured is the kavod, the glory, "the chariot, not the Rider". Matter, evil and the purpose of the world (III:8-15). Matter hides. Evil is an absence, not a thing. Most evil a person meets he makes himself.

family: The Rambam: one G-d, known by negation, loved by knowing
title: The Guide for the Perplexed, Part Two: how the range builds the one idea
abstract: Part Two has three subjects, and one thread runs through them: G-d acts by will, not by necessity, and He acts through things. G-d proved (II:1-2). Twenty-five premises from Aristotle, one more granted for the sake of argument (that motion is eternal), and four proofs: the first mover, the necessary being, the one who brings potential into act, and the argument from the world's being one. Whatever the world's origin, "the existence of G-d, His unity and His not being a body" follow. The intelligences and creation (II:3-31).

family: The Rambam: one G-d, known by negation, loved by knowing
title: The Letters and the Book of the Commandments
abstract: Iggeret Teiman (1172). To the Jews of Yemen under forced conversion and a false messiah. Why the Torah is attacked (by the sword, by argument, by imitation); why it cannot be destroyed; Sinai as the ground of faith; against calculating the end and against astrology; how to treat the false messiah. Treatise on Resurrection (1191). Written because readers took his teaching on the World to Come as a denial of resurrection.

family: The Kuzari: the G-d of Abraham, known by taste
title: The Kuzari: the G-d of Abraham, known by taste and served in joy
abstract: The Kuzari is a talk between the king of the Khazars and a Jewish sage, the Chaver. The king keeps dreaming that an angel tells him: "your intention is pleasing to the Creator, but your deed is not" (line 1). The whole book answers that dream. Its teaching on the unity of G-d has four parts. He is known first by meeting, not by proof.

family: The Kuzari: the G-d of Abraham, known by taste
title: Kuzari, part 3 (lines 205-278): the pious man's day
abstract: The king has heard enough theory. He asks: what does the pious man among you do today? Part 3 is the answer, and it is the most practical part of the book: a whole day, a whole week and a whole year of a person who serves G-d without leaving the world. Then it turns to a long defense of the Oral Torah against the Karaites, and ends with the chain of the sages.

family: The Kuzari: the G-d of Abraham, known by taste
title: Kuzari, parts 1 and 2 (lines 1-204)
abstract: The book is a talk between a king and a sage. The king of the Khazars keeps having the same dream. An angel tells him: your intention is pleasing to the Creator, but your deeds are not. He asks a philosopher, a Christian and a Muslim, and last, with little hope, a Jew, called "the Chaver" (the companion, the learned friend). Part 1 is the case for the Torah: why the Chaver starts from what happened, not from a proof.

family: The Kuzari: the G-d of Abraham, known by taste
title: Kuzari, parts 4 and 5 (lines 279-350): the G-d of Abraham and the G-d of Aristotle
abstract: Part 4 goes back to the Names and reaches the book's most famous line: the difference between "Elokim" and the four-letter Name is the difference between the G-d of Aristotle and the G-d of Abraham. Then it shows how the prophet sees, how the other faiths stand, what Sefer Yetzirah teaches, and what science the sages had. Part 5 gives the king what he asks for, a short course in the philosophers' physics and psychology, and then takes it apart.

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: The Zohar on Bereshit (volume I): overview for the understanding layer
abstract: Part 1 of four. This covers the whole of Zohar volume I as Sefaria gives it: the Hakdamah (Introduction), the Zohar on the twelve portions of Genesis, and the Addenda to volume I. Line numbers are those of zohar/_text/part1-zohar-bereshit.txt (one segment per line, "ref, tab, text"). Quotes are given as «Aramaic» (Sefaria ref; line N). What we draw is marked (ours). Tanya and Chabad references in these files are given from memory and are marked "memory"; they were not checked against the Tanya text in this pass.

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: The Zohar on Shemot (volume II): overview for the understanding layer
abstract: Part 2 of four. This covers the whole of Zohar volume II as Sefaria gives it: Shemot, Vaera, Bo, Beshalach, Yitro, Mishpatim, Terumah, Sifra DiTzniuta (which sits inside Terumah in this edition), Tetzaveh, Ki Tisa, Vayakhel, Pekudei (with the Palaces of holiness and of impurity), and the Addenda to volume II. Line numbers are those of zohar/_text/zohar-part2.txt. What we draw is marked (ours).

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar, part 1: the Hakdamah (Introduction)
abstract: The Introduction (Hakdamah) opens the printed Zohar. It is not one teaching but a chain of openings, stories and night talks: the rose among thorns; "Who created these" (Mi and Mah); the letters that came before God asking to be the letter of creation; the donkey driver who turns out to be the son of Rav Hamnuna Sava; the night of the bride (the Shavuot night); and, at the end, Rabbi Shimon's list of the first fourteen commandments read out of the first chapter of Genesis.

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar, part 1: Bereshit I (the first days)
abstract: This is the Zohar's reading of the first verses of Genesis, and it is the densest cosmology in the whole work. It opens with the "spark of darkness" (botzina dekardinuta) and the point that breaks out of Ein Sof, walks through the six days as the unfolding of the sefirot, then holds several long passages in the later style of the Tikkunei Zohar and Ra'aya Meheimna (lines 444-557: prayer and the shofar notes, the mixed multitude, Moses and the Shechinah in exile), and returns to "Bereshit" in a second, parallel …

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar, part 1: Bereshit II (light in darkness, the Garden, the seven palaces of prayer)
abstract: This range goes on through the days of creation, the Garden, the serpent, Cain and Abel and the book of Adam; then comes one of the great set pieces of the Zohar, the Heichalot (palaces): seven palaces in the Garden of Eden below for the souls of the righteous (lines 746-801), and seven palaces of holiness through which a prayer rises, spirit into spirit, until "all is one will to Ein Sof" (lines 802-888). The range ends with a short second reading of the days and of Shabbat (889-931).

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar, part 1: Bereshit III (Shabbat, the flame, the serpent, Enoch, the flood generation)
abstract: The last part of the Zohar on Bereshit. It holds the Zohar's Shabbat teaching (the "sukkah of peace" spread over the world), a long passage on man and woman read upward, Rabbi Shimon's walk to Tiberias with Rabbi Pinchas, the contemplation of the flame (lines 989-1010), the serpent and the undoing of Sinai, Cain and Abel, Adam's book, Enoch taken early, God's grief over the wicked, and the generation of Enosh and the flood.

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar, part 1: Noach
abstract: The Zohar on Noah reads the righteous man and the ark as the foundation (Yesod) and the Shechinah; the flood as the lower world falling back into "water in water"; Noah's hiding from the destroyer; Moses who gave his life for his people against Noah who did not pray for his generation; the rainbow; Noah's vineyard; Nimrod; and the tower of Babel as a craft of wisdom turned to "another authority". It includes several Tosefta and Sitrei Torah pieces. All 388 lines were read in full.

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar, part 1: Lech Lecha
abstract: The Zohar on Abraham is the Zohar's portrait of the seeker. Abraham weighs every power that rules the world and cannot reach the one at the center; when God sees his longing, He reveals Himself. Around that story the range sets the soul's ascent (nefesh, ruach, neshamah, read through the lamp), the soul's life at night and after death, "go down to Egypt and come up", midnight study, the blessing that needs a vessel, Rabbi Yosei ben Pazi who came to Torah for money and found love, and a long …

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar, part 1: Vayera
abstract: Vayera is Abraham at the tent door: the three guests, the escort, the plea for Sodom, Lot and his daughters, Abimelech, the birth of Isaac, Hagar, and the binding. The Zohar layers in much Midrash HaNe'elam (the "hidden midrash"), which reads the same verses as the soul at death and at the resurrection, and a vision of the end. All 513 lines were read in full. Every quote below printed "FOUND near line N" from find_he.py verify on the export.

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar, part 1: Chayei Sara
abstract: Chayei Sara is the Zohar's book of the soul and the body, of death and burial and the resurrection. Its Midrash HaNe'elam sections read Abraham as the soul, Sarah and Rebecca as the body, Eliezer as the angel who restores the body, and the buying of the cave as the soul's care for its body.

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar, part 1: Toldot
abstract: Toldot is the Zohar's book of Jacob and Esau, of the wells, and of the stolen blessings. Inside it: the world, the body and the Torah as one body of limbs; the moon that shines only when it sees the sun; those who stand in the house of God at night; God pairing a hard one with a soft one so the world can bear itself; a Midrash HaNe'elam on the heart and the liver; the righteous tested so their heads are raised; the wells as the work of faith …

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar, part 1: Vayetzei
abstract: Vayetzei follows Jacob out of Beersheba to Haran and back. The Zohar reads his road as the sun going down to its place, as the soul going down into "the other side" and coming out whole, and as Israel going into exile. Inside it: the ladder set on earth whose head reaches heaven; "surely God is in this place and I did not know"; the well that rises to meet the one it is bound to; the hidden world (Leah) and the revealed world (Rachel); the power of thought over …

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar, part 1: Vayishlach
abstract: Vayishlach is Jacob meeting Esau and the angel at night. The Zohar makes it a book of prayer: the righteous who do not lean on their merits but on prayer; the prayer of the poor that breaks through every gate; how to order a prayer (praise, then request; spoken words and the words that stay in the heart); the prayer of many that becomes a crown.

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar, part 1: Vayeshev
abstract: Vayeshev is Joseph's fall: the coat, the dreams, the pit, Tamar, Potiphar's wife, the prison and the dreams of the butler and baker. The Zohar reads it around one hard question: why do the righteous suffer? Its answers here are among the most tender in the book: the broken share the moon's lack and she dwells in them; "sufferings of love"; the Shechinah goes with the righteous into the valley of death.

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar, part 1: Miketz
abstract: Miketz is Joseph raised from the pit to rule Egypt, and his brothers coming down for bread. The Zohar uses it to teach how a person lives inside God's hidden plan: all Israel held on one tree of life; the good that is done "in its time"; rejoicing in whatever comes; the small sins a person tramples underfoot without noticing; not watching one's own prayer to see if it is answered; the evil inclination that lives only where there is wine-joy and pride; and above all, not repaying evil.

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar, part 1: Vayigash
abstract: Vayigash is Judah stepping forward to Joseph, the brothers' reunion, and Jacob's spirit reviving. The Zohar reads "and Judah drew near" as the drawing near of two worlds, king to king, and of the soul's levels to each other. Inside it: nefesh, ruach and neshamah as three rungs a person climbs; David who slept "sixty breaths" so as never to taste death and rose at midnight, "living to the Living"; the prayer spoken in a whisper that is always accepted; Elijah's still small voice; the Shechinah weeping for her children …

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar, part 1: Vayechi I
abstract: Vayechi is the book of Jacob's last seventeen years and his death. This first part opens (lines 4409-4512) with a text in an unusual Aramaic about exile and redemption that ends with the printed note «עד כאן אינו מן הזהר» (Vayechi 15:5; line 4512): "until here it is not from the Zohar." It was read in full and is reported below, marked as a later insert.

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar, part 1: Vayechi II
abstract: The second half of Vayechi is Jacob's blessing of Joseph's sons and of the twelve tribes, his death, and his burial. It is the longest single range in this volume and one of the richest. The Zohar here gives its plainest statement of unity (thought, understanding, voice and speech are one, and thought is bound to Ayin and never parts from it); the soul as a prince sent to a village to be raised and brought home by the Queen; the days of a life woven into garments; the command …

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar, part 1: Addenda to Volume I
abstract: The Addenda (hashmatot, "omissions") are pieces that printers gathered at the end of Volume I: short Zohar passages on Genesis that were missing from the main text, passages from the Ra'aya Mehemna ("Faithful Shepherd") layer, pieces marked as Sitrei Torah and Zohar Yashan, and some Hebrew fragments drawn from the Sefer HaBahir and a Midrash on Ruth. Much of it is dense sefirotic mapping of the days of creation and the Temple offerings.

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar on Shemot: the Shekhinah goes into exile with them
abstract: Parashat Shemot in the Zohar is a book of exile. It opens with the tree of life whose colors "settle and do not settle" when they go down into a light that does not shine (lines 1-5), and asks one question over and over: when Israel goes down, who goes down with them? The answer, given a dozen ways, is that the Shekhinah (the indwelling Presence) goes down, with all the hosts of heaven, and that God Himself weeps.

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar on Vaera and Bo: the voice without its word, and the One without form
abstract: Vaera (lines 397-602) turns on God's words to Moses, "I appeared to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob as El Shaddai, but by My name YHVH I was not known to them." The Zohar reads it as a teaching about two kinds of seeing (lines 417-425), about Moses as a "voice" whose "word" is in exile (lines 462-468), and about the unity of opposites in the four elements (lines 428-446). A Raya Mehemna ("Faithful Shepherd") passage sets out the first commandment, to know God "in general and in detail" (lines 451-460).

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar on Beshalach: the sea, the song, and bread from heaven day by day
abstract: Beshalach follows Israel from Egypt to the sea, through the Song, into the desert, to the manna and to the war with Amalek. The Zohar's main blocks:

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar on Yitro: the hidden trace, the faces of a person, and the voice at Sinai
abstract: Jethro (lines 1335-1395). Why the Torah could be given only after Jethro, the chief priest of every idol, came and said "now I know that the Lord is greater than all gods": when the other side bows, "the Holy One rules alone above and below". Balaam and Job as Pharaoh's other two advisers. The mountain open to anyone who wants. * A Tosefta on the hidden trace (lines 1368-1372). * The "Raza deRazin", the secret of secrets (lines 1396-1568).

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar on Mishpatim: the Old Man's journey, the maiden in the palace, and the kiss
abstract: Most of this range (lines 1910-2279) is the Sava deMishpatim, one of the Zohar's great set pieces. R. Chiya and R. Yosi meet an old donkey driver on the road, a man R. Yosi thought was full of empty riddles. At the inn he wraps himself in his cloak and, over one long night, reads the laws of the Hebrew slave and the sold daughter ("these are the judgments") as the secrets of the soul: its coming down into a body, its oppression, its return, reincarnation and levirate marriage, the …

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar on Terumah, first half: the order of prayer, the Shema, the kiss, and the soul after death
abstract: Terumah is the longest parashah in the Zohar. Its first half is not really about the Tabernacle at all. The command "take for Me an offering" (Exodus 25:2) opens onto almost everything: the hidden point that comes out of Ein Sof (line 2499), and the "canopy" (apiryon) of Shabbat (lines 2510-2523); * what it costs to acquire a mitzvah, a teacher, a friend, and the Holy Spirit (lines 2524-2531); * bringing a wicked man back, which is greater than giving to the poor (lines 2530-2541); * the whole order of …

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar on Terumah, second half: the table, the menorah, the gate of tears, and 'all is one'
abstract: The second half of Terumah moves through the vessels of the Tabernacle, but each one opens onto the life of an ordinary person: the town where the angel of death has no power, and the letter tet (lines 2957-2970); * the table: a person's own table as an altar, eating before God, blessing after food, the cup of blessing (lines 2975-3025, 3046-3062, 3259-3277); * a donkey driver named Chanan who teaches on "a time to act for God" (lines 3026-3050); * a Raya Mehemna on the menorah, the ark, and …

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar: Sifra DiTzniuta, Tetzaveh and Ki Tisa: the hidden One, light out of darkness, and the son in exile
abstract: Sifra DiTzniuta, "the Book of Concealment" (lines 3416-3488), sits in this volume at the end of Terumah. It is five short chapters in a compressed, riddling Aramaic, the seed text that the Idra Rabba and Idra Zuta later open. It speaks of the "scale" that was set up before the worlds, the "skull" of the Ancient One, the thirteen features of the beard (the thirteen attributes of mercy), the letters of the Name, and the "kings who died".

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar on Vayakhel: the path of prayer, Shabbat's added soul, and the Shema to Ein Sof
abstract: Vayakhel is the Zohar's great parashah of prayer and Shabbat. Its main parts: Moses gathers Israel apart from the mixed multitude after the calf (lines 3755-3796), with a passage on the angel of death at funerals that we set aside; * Elijah and Jonah; Jonah as the soul's voyage through life and death (lines 3797-3851); * the poor man as God's gift, and Jacob's trust (lines 3815-3827); * the order of prayer as the Queen adorned and brought to the King, ending in giving over the soul (lines 3861-3872); * …

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar on Pekudei, first half: the counted and the hidden, the work that finishes itself, and Ein Sof beyond will
abstract: Pekudei, "the accounts," closes the book of Exodus. In the Zohar it is very long, because it holds the two sets of Heikhalot, the seven palaces of holiness and the seven of impurity. This first report covers the part before them (lines 4251-4720): the daily voice that calls "guard yourselves" and the light hidden for the righteous (lines 4253-4258); * the census and the question of blessing on what is counted (lines 4262-4347); * the building that finished itself, and Betzalel "in the shade of God" (lines 4288-4309); * the …

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar on Pekudei, second half: the Heikhalot, the palaces of prayer and their shadows
abstract: The Heikhalot of Pekudei are the Zohar's map of the ascent of prayer and of the soul. There are two sets. Seven palaces of holiness (lines 4721-5085): (1) the palace of the "sapphire brick," where prayers and souls are received or turned back, and the gate of tears; (2) the palace of "the essence of heaven," where the garments of the soul are kept and the reward for seeking wisdom is given; (3) the palace of "radiance," with gates for decrees, for life and death, for illness, and for healing …

family: The Zohar, volumes I and II
title: Zohar, Addenda to Volume II: seeing the voices, the hidden thought, and the child who stills anger
abstract: The Addenda are loose pieces that the printers placed after Pekudei. Some are Hebrew, some Aramaic. They are: Sinai (5210-5216): the people "saw the voices." There were seven voices, and out of them came one word. Twelve commands to do and twelve to guard (5217-5218). The first is the unity of G-d. The last is to give one's soul over in cleaving.
