title: Methods for reaching the animal soul: the Rebbe Rayatz (slice RY)
abstract: Every Hebrew/Yiddish quote below passed find_he.py verify FILE "…" --line N with FOUND near line N. OCR quotes keep the scan's spelling (for example ס for ם, יי for quotation marks, נ for ן). "Stated" means the source says it. "Ours" means it is our reading.

family: The animal soul: how a G-dly idea reaches it
title: Methods for the animal soul: the Tzemach Tzedek and the Rebbe Maharash (slice TZ)
abstract: Notes. IK lines 1183-1204 are letters headed "ספק למי" (recipient uncertain) in the Tzemach Tzedek's Igros. TS lines 10864, 11960, 12910, 12959 are notes of the Maharash's talks written by the Rebbe Rashab (הנחות). SHS is a Rayatz retelling of the Tzemach Tzedek.

family: The animal soul: how a G-dly idea reaches it
title: Methods slice RS: the Rebbe Rashab
abstract: Works used: Kuntres Umaayan (U, clean text), Kuntres HaAvodah (KA, OCR), Kuntres HaTefillah (KT, OCR), Kuntres Eitz HaChaim (EH, OCR), Igros Kodesh (IK, OCR), Hemshech Ayin Beis (AB, typed), Hemshech Samach Vav (SV, OCR), Sefer HaMaamarim (SM, OCR, sampled), Toras Shalom (TS; the file here is the responsa volume, see §4).

family: The animal soul: how a G-dly idea reaches it
title: RM: the Lubavitcher Rebbe — ways to bring G-dly ideas to the animal soul
abstract: Slice: the Lubavitcher Rebbe's works in Chassidus-txt/R. Menachem Mendel Schneerson (Lubavitcher Rebbe) (1902-1994)/. Builds on animal-soul/SOURCES.md (P1-P20) and darkei-hachassidus/sources-b-rayatz-rebbe.md. Lines already used there (TM 101889, 20179, 44255, 107862, 36420, 108753, 21802; MM 683; HY 56, 314, 332-335) are not repeated as main quotes.

family: The animal soul: how a G-dly idea reaches it
title: Slice MR: the Mitteler Rebbe (and R. Aharon of Strashelye)
abstract: Already covered in SOURCES.md (P4, P7, P9, P10, P11): the natural soul's five-rung ladder, the business analogy, "great toil", the two souls' arousals. This file builds on that and adds the rest of the slice.

family: The animal soul: how a G-dly idea reaches it
title: The animal soul in contemplation: what the sources say
abstract: Terms used throughout: - Animal soul (נפש הבהמית, נה"ב): the soul that gives the body life and wants what the body wants. Chassidus also calls it the natural soul (נפש הטבעית, נה"ט) and the living soul (החיונית). - Natural mind (שכל הטבעי, השכל הטבעי דנה"ב): the animal soul's own intelligence. It is real intelligence, but it works only on physical things and on what serves the self. - Human intellect (שכל אנושי): ordinary human reasoning. Some sources put it in the animal soul.

family: The animal soul: how a G-dly idea reaches it
title: The animal soul: the psychology, and what convinces it that it is held
abstract: The three strongest bridges (our judgment). (1) A checkable fact set beside the awake old belief (3.1, 3.6), which is memale said concretely. (2) Repetition tied to daily cues (3.13), which is the tradition's blessings. (3) Close before vast (3.9), which is the Rashab's own order of memale for the animal soul and sovev for the G-dly soul.

family: The animal soul: how a G-dly idea reaches it
title: Ways for the animal soul: everything is being held
abstract: The owner: "One of the key parts of hisbonenus is coming up with different ways to understand that everything is being held by G-d, in the human brain, in the animal soul." The animal soul (the natural soul) is the life of the body. It wants what is good for me: life, warmth, safety, pleasure, standing, control. It is not evil, and it can be turned (Chassidus Unity Index/consciousness-map/MAP.md line 27). It thinks in concrete, physical, self-interested terms, so it is not reached by abstractions.

family: Being held
title: Being held: the psychology
abstract: The teaching, in one line. Everything, you included, is being given its being by G-d right now. You are not the one holding yourself or your world up (FRAMEWORK U1; the Baal Shem Tov's reading in Shaar HaYichud VehaEmunah 1, quoted there as Q01). The trouble it answers.

family: Being held
title: Being held: the Baal Shem Tov and his circle
abstract: Sources outside Chabad: the Baal Shem Tov (Besht) as his students report him, the Maggid of Mezritch, R. Yaakov Yosef of Polonne, the Degel (the Besht's grandson), R. Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, R. Menachem Nachum of Chernobyl, R. Pinchas of Koretz, R. Elimelech of Lizhensk, the Apter Rav, R. Kalonymus Kalman of Krakow (Maor VaShemesh), R. Chaim Chaykl of Amdur, the Radziner, and the Piaseczno Rebbe. Also Chovos HaLevavos, Shaar HaBitachon (the Gate of Trust), the older book these masters build on.

family: Being held
title: Being held: the Chabad sources
abstract: "Shaar HaYichud" below, with no other name, means the Alter Rebbe's Shaar HaYichud VehaEmunah, the second part of the Tanya (TANYA lines 766-883). The Mitteler Rebbe's book of the same name is called "the Gate of Unity" (GOU).

family: Being held
title: The glass wall: the goal of every conversation
abstract: The Alter Rebbe (Torah Or; "From hearing to seeing" in the guide's library) separates two ways of knowing the same truth. Hearing. Understanding it well, thinking it through deeply, even believing it firmly; "but it is still like news heard from others," so "when he takes his mind off it even for a moment he turns to his desires." This is the glass wall: the idea is true, agreed with, and outside. Seeing.

family: Being held
title: The root: not held, so holding everything up
abstract: In the owner's words, about drinking: "The core problem of addiction isn't the alcohol. The alcohol is actually the solution to their problem. The real problem is that they feel alone, and existentially they feel they have to hold the world up. They don't feel held and contained. There's a lack of containment, from childhood wounds, and really from existence itself there's a certain pain. Chassidus goes to the root of the problem, which is realizing that you are contained.

family: The Chassidic clinic: how a mashpia reads and treats a person
title: DX: the diagnostic framework. How a mashpia reads a person
abstract: The sources already diagnose. Tanya ch. 25-31 is a differential diagnosis: it sorts heaviness by what it is about (worldly things, sins, stray thoughts, or nothing at all), by when it falls (at prayer or at work), and by whether there is life in it (bitterness) or none (sadness); and it gives each kind its own remedy and its own hour. Kuntres HaHitpa'alut grades how a person hears (from 'wants only to be moved' to 'true but far from me').

family: The Chassidic clinic: how a mashpia reads and treats a person
title: BODY: the body inside the avodah
abstract: The owner asked the guide about afternoon tiredness, then about supplements, and got: "your body too, take care of it." True, but it puts the body beside the practice instead of inside it. As the Maggid says, a small hole in the body is a big hole in the soul. This file makes the body one avodah with the soul: every body act gets its place inside a stage, its reason from the sources, and its words for the guide.

family: The Chassidic clinic: how a mashpia reads and treats a person
title: P1 · Protocols part 1: the Chassidic clinic
abstract: Each protocol is what a mashpia would hold in mind for one kind of person. It has a formulation (where it sits in the soul, which state on the map, how it traces to the root problem of a self that holds itself up, what is blocked, what state is needed, and which kind of healing fits) and a protocol of 4 stages.

family: The Chassidic clinic: how a mashpia reads and treats a person
title: P2 · The clinic, protocols part 2
abstract: What this is. For each problem, a master's formulation (where in the soul, what state, how it traces to the root, what is blocked, what state is needed, what kind of healing) and a staged treatment path, each stage with its exact practice, signs, the fallback when stuck, and when to move on. Each stage ends with what the guide says to start the person on it (80-140 words, plain, no Hebrew or book names).

family: The psychological parallel to hisbonenus
title: The psychological parallel, Part A: where hisbonenus sits, and steps 1-7
abstract: It is a guideline and a check for the builders. It tells us which parts of the ladder line up with things psychology has measured, what those studies found, how strong the findings are, and what that suggests for how the guide describes a step, words a question, or watches for trouble. It is not the guide's voice. The guide never speaks in therapy terms, never names these constructs to a person, and never refers anyone to therapy outside danger (the owner's rule; FOUNDATIONS.md §1).

family: The psychological parallel to hisbonenus
title: The psychological parallel, part B: steps 8-14, and adverse effects and counterfeits
abstract: What this is, and what it is not. This is a parallel academic map for the builders: a guideline and a check. It is not the guide's voice and it does not replace the Chassidic content. The guide never speaks in therapy terms. It never sends anyone to therapy outside real danger. It is not mindfulness. Nothing here claims that psychology "proves" Chassidus. Where the two meet, we say so. Where they only look alike, we say exactly how they differ.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: The Medicine Map · Tier A
abstract: Each condition's entry gives: what it looks like from inside; what the library says is really going on; the false conclusions a person draws and what the works set against them; the programs (steps, timing, who for, who not for); the reframes; where the Rebbeim agree and differ; cautions; key passages in Hebrew and English; one to three candidate truths for the guide; and what the core works do not cover.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: The Chabad Library as Medicine
abstract: The Rebbe Rashab's Toras Shalom as held here is his halachic responsa, so it moved to Tier C.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: Anger and relationships
abstract: Someone wronged me and it replays. When I'm hurt I hold it forever. I quietly hate certain people. He owes me, so why should I do right by him? What is really going on. Tanya: rancour is a rising of the heart, and the mind by its nature can rule it and act the very opposite, with kindness and patience toward the one who wronged you. Anger is a moment when faith has left: had he believed this came from God, he would not be angry.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: BT · Biurei Tanya (Esterman, Kaidaner, Simchovitz)
abstract: What it is. Three commentaries on Tanya by chassidim who taught it. Esterman is the longest. It glosses phrase by phrase and often says what a line means "in avodah." Its introduction argues that Chassidus made inner work (the soul's service) the main thing, where earlier musar worked on the body's actions. Kaidaner gives long answers to hard questions in the Tanya, above all on sadness versus bitterness and on who can be a beinoni.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: CA · Chanah Ariel
abstract: What it is. Derushim on the weekly parsha and the festivals by a leading mashpia who studied under the Alter Rebbe and the Mitteler Rebbe. Most of it is dense Kabbalah: partzufim, Tohu and Tikkun, nogah, the unifications. Scattered through it, often as "and so it is in avodas Hashem", are sharp practical passages.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: Checks · Tier A
abstract: 975 of 975 passages found in their source files (letters-only match; nikud, punctuation and spacing ignored). 975 found at the line the reader gave, or within two lines of it; 0 found on a different line (the reader's line number was off; the text is there). 0 not found.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: Desire and habit
abstract: ## C10 · I feel like a fraud because I still want what I've renounced Everyone thinks I'm good, but inside the cravings are as strong as ever. I'm only forcing myself. I pray with real feeling, then walk out and want the world. I must be a hypocrite. What is really going on. Tanya gives the core: the in-between person (beinoni) keeps the evil in him at full strength.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: DM · Derech Mitzvosecha
abstract: What it is. This is the Tzemach Tzedek's book on the inner reasons of the commandments. Each section starts from the halachic definition (Rambam, Chinuch) and asks what the commandment does at its root, mostly in Lurianic terms: sefiros, vessels, drawing down the light of Ein Sof. It ends with a long essay on the root of prayer and Shema, several discourses, and supplements. Most of it is cosmology and Kabbalah.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: Ego and self
abstract: All is well. I avoid serious sins, I feel nothing missing, and nothing holds me back. If anyone is sick, it's the others. I don't notice that my heart is somewhere else entirely. What is really going on. The library reads 'I'm fine' as blindness, not health. Sha'arei Teshuvah and Sha'arei Avodah: without knowledge (daas) a person cannot tell light from dark and imagines himself whole; adding knowledge brings feeling, and feeling brings return.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: Faith and meaning
abstract: ## C09 · I doubt that my faith and devotion are real Is my devotion real, or just my personality? My love is mixed with self-interest, so it must be fake. I slip, so maybe I don't love God. I don't trust what I feel, and sometimes I doubt I believe at all. What is really going on. Sha'arei Avodah (R.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: Fear and worry
abstract: ## C16 · Constant worry about money, health and family Worry about livelihood, the children, my health, wakes up with me and follows me into prayer. I scheme and plan as if everything depends on me, and I run from adviser to adviser for answers. What is really going on. The library does not treat worry as prudence. It treats it as a burden carried in the wrong place.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: GU · Sha'ar HaYichud (The Gate of Unity)
abstract: What it is. The author calls it the "kuntres of contemplation": a short guide to how a person brings divine unity into a mind and heart that can hold it, across every level from the first tzimtzum to this world. The first eighth teaches the anatomy of contemplation. It covers what real iyun (sustained study) is, how daat binds a person to an idea, and how tevunah carries an idea out into the heart and into prayer.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: HY · Hayom Yom
abstract: What it is. A daily calendar of about 600 very short entries, one per day of the year. The Rebbe compiled it (1942-43) from talks, letters and stories of the previous Rebbes. Each day gives a custom or point of liturgy, a date in Chabad history, and usually one saying: a practical, distilled piece of avodah (inner work). The aim is to put a short line of Chassidus in a person's hand every day and to shape his day, prayer, livelihood and relations with others.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: IB · Imrei Binah
abstract: What it is. The Mitteler Rebbe gathers his father's teachings on the Shema and adds his own explanations. The work is organized as gates: Kerias Shema, Tzitzis and Tefillin. The author states its aim himself: in hard times, give ordinary people a way to settle the unity of God, the higher unity (Havaya) and the lower unity (Elokim), into mind and heart, so their souls can find rest. The introduction and the opening gate press that deep contemplation is required of everyone, each by his capacity.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: INY · Inyanah Shel Toras HaChassidus (On the Essence of Chassidus)
abstract: What it is. This is the Rebbe's essay on what Chassidus essentially is. The virtues usually listed for it are waking the world from a faint, going beyond the letter of the law, changing the nature of one's traits, and making Godliness graspable to anyone. The Rebbe says these are only branches of one essential point. Chassidus draws down the Ein Sof itself. It is the yechidah (the essence of the soul) of the Torah, just as Moshiach is the yechidah of the world.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: KA · Kuntres HaAvodah
abstract: What it is. A short manual (7 chapters, c.1909-10) for young men beginning the "service of the heart", prayer with contemplation. It argues that the aim of prayer's labor is love of G-d, which both binds the soul to G-d and refines the animal soul. Fear (acceptance of the yoke) is required at all times as its foundation. Most of its practical force goes to diagnosing false service: an excitement that leaves no mark, general contemplation that breeds bitterness, going cold at the start, reaching above one's level.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: KH · Kuntres HaHispaalus (Tract on Ecstasy)
abstract: What it is. Two pastoral letters from 1814 to the Chassidim. The first is short: people are worn down by earning a living, many are close to despair, and he offers to travel and hold study gatherings for followers who live far away. The second is the Kuntres itself, a detailed guide to the feelings that contemplation and prayer produce.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: KT · Kuntres HaTefillah
abstract: What it is. A short open letter (1900) from the Rebbe Rashab to his Chassidim, who kept asking "how does one pray?" It says prayer, the service of the heart, is the core of inner work. Learning Chassidus is only preparation. The heart and character actually change only when that learning is contemplated at length and in detail during prayer. The work diagnoses several "illnesses" it sees among Chassidim, gives five preparations for prayer, and adds separate tracks for beginners, busy businessmen and everyone.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: KU · Kuntres Umaayan
abstract: What it is. Twenty-eight short maamarim on the verse "A spring shall come out of the house of G-d and water the valley of Shittim." It reads shittim as shtus, a spirit of folly. The work is a clinical anatomy of how the yetzer fools a person: indulgence, "it won't cut me off", excuses, crediting oneself, pride, and the overbusy merchant. Each folly is exposed by reasoning.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: LS1 · Likkutei Sichos
abstract: What it is. Edited talks on the weekly Torah portions and the festivals, plus appended letters. A typical sicha raises a precise question about the wording in Rashi, Rambam, a Midrash or a halacha, resolves it, then often ends with a lesson "for our deeds and service now" (הוראה). The lessons mostly direct the reader toward spreading Torah, Ahavat Yisrael, teshuvah and yearning for redemption. The appended letters give direct personal counsel, some of it to people who are frightened about illness.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: LS2 · Likkutei Sichos
abstract: What it is. Edited talks of the Rebbe arranged by weekly portion. Most sichos take a close question in Rashi, Rambam or halacha, solve it, then draw a lesson for inner work (avodah) and a directive (hora'ah). Each volume ends with an appendix of letters. The letters are short, practical answers to individuals, and vol. 36's appendix is a collection on health: body and soul, surgery, medicines, nerves, depression and mental illness.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: LS3 · Likkutei Sichos
abstract: What it is. Weekly talks (sichos) on Vayikra, Bamidbar and Devarim, as the Rebbe edited them. Each one works through a close problem in Rashi, the Rambam or halacha and ends with a lesson for inner service. Volume 39 adds long commentaries on his father's notes to Iggeres HaTeshuvah. Each volume has a section of letters, sorted by parsha. The letters are where the Rebbe answers individuals who are sad, despairing, bereaved, worried about money or health, or stuck in their return.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: LT1 · Likkutei Torah
abstract: What it is. This is a collection of the Alter Rebbe's maamarim (discourses) on the weekly portions, edited with many cross-references. Each discourse opens with a verse or a saying of the Sages, lays out its Kabbalistic structure (sefiros, the worlds, arousal from below and from above), and then usually turns in a paragraph or two to 'the service of man'. That turn gives short, sharp teachings on prayer, teshuvah, bitterness versus sadness, foreign thoughts, inspiration that fades, anger and desire.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: LT2 · Likkutei Torah
abstract: What it is. The Alter Rebbe's maamarim on the weekly portions from Korach to Nitzavim, edited by the Tzemach Tzedek with cross-references and glosses. Each discourse opens with a verse or a saying of the Sages, lays out Kabbalistic structure (sefirot, surrounding and indwelling light, shells), and often turns to avodah: prayer, Torah study, teshuvah, love and awe.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: LT3 · Likkutei Torah
abstract: What it is. A collection of maamarim the Alter Rebbe delivered on the festivals, edited by the Tzemach Tzedek, who added a dense web of cross-references. This part covers the High Holidays, Sukkot and Shir HaShirim. Each maamar opens from a verse or a teaching of the Sages, builds a Kabbalistic structure (the surrounding and the indwelling light, the thirteen attributes of mercy, keter, and so on), and then turns to "avodah," the inner service that brings that structure down into the person.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: MST · Sha'arei Teshuvah (Gates of Return)
abstract: What it is. A manual in two parts for "people pressed by their business who long to bring their hearts close to their Father in Heaven." It teaches how teshuvah of the heart (bitterness, a broken heart) and prayer of the heart (joy, love, contemplation) depend on each other. Teshuvah comes before prayer as its foundation. The work names the ways the heart is blocked (dullness, desire, worry about livelihood, stray thoughts, coldness) and gives the matching work for each.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: PR · Pelach HaRimon
abstract: What it is. A collection of R. Hillel of Paritch's explanations of maamarim, arranged by the parsha cycle from Vayikra to Behaalosecha. Much of it is his notes of talks by the Mitteler Rebbe and the Tzemach Tzedek, with his own commentary added. Its aim is to lay out the Kabbalistic structure of the festivals and mitzvos (Pesach, the Omer, Shavuos, Yom Kippur) and to trace each one into avodah, the inner work of prayer, teshuvah and bittul.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: Prayer and connection
abstract: ## C01 · I understand it, but my heart feels nothing I've learned it, I can explain it, I even believe it. But when I pray, nothing stirs. It stays in my head and never reaches my heart, and when I try to feel something it feels fake. What is really going on. Every work here treats knowing without feeling as a known condition, not a verdict on the person.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: Purpose and service
abstract: ## C40 · My ordinary life feels spiritually empty Only prayer and study seem to count; my work day is dead time. I'm alive but not living. I'd rather soar in lofty spiritual heights than deal with what's in front of me. What is really going on. The condition has two faces, and the works answer both. On the empty ordinary: Tanya says the world exists because God wanted a dwelling in the lowest place, so the working day is the very site of the purpose.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: Return after failure
abstract: I've tried so hard for so long and nothing has changed, so why keep fighting? It's hopeless. And since I'll never be good anyway, I might as well do what I want. What is really going on. The works read despair not as a clear view of the truth but as a mechanism, and often as a disguise. Biurei Tanya: sadness says 'no hope' to the soul and then gives permission: 'I'm not a tzaddik anyway, so I'll do what my heart wants'.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: SA · Sha'arei Avodah (Gates of Divine Service)
abstract: What it is. A systematic manual of avodah by the Alter Rebbe's student. The introduction says that the verse "know today and bring it back to your heart" contains all of service in three parts: knowing (mind), the heart (love, fear, the heart's will) and deed (Torah and mitzvot). None of them works without the others. The author writes because people each seize one part: some take knowledge and reject feeling, some take feeling and reject knowledge, some take deed alone.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: Sadness and heaviness
abstract: ## C13 · A heavy, gloomy mood and a dark lens on everything I wake up heavy, sad and irritable for no reason. I'm melancholy by nature. The future looks dark and I only notice what's missing. Even joy comes out heavy. What is really going on. The library separates kinds of heaviness. Kuntres HaHispaalus sets the natural soul's melancholy over bodily lack against the soul's grief at distance from God, which can turn to joy. The Rebbe Rayatz names a temperament 'on a line of sadness'.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: SHS1 · Sefer HaSichos (Rayatz), 5680-5691 (1920-1931)
abstract: What it is. This is a collection of the Rebbe Rayatz's talks, mostly in Yiddish and written down by listeners, from farbrengens in Soviet Russia and later Riga (1920-1931). The talks move between stories of earlier Rebbes and chassidim, replies to people at the table, communal urgings about Torah study under persecution, and short Chassidus teachings. It also contains his first-person diary of his 1927 arrest in Spalerno prison, and biographical notes.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: SHS2 · Sefer HaSichos (Rayatz), 5706-5710
abstract: What it is. Transcripts of the Rebbe Rayatz's farbrengen talks, yechidus remarks and a few written reshimos from his American years. Most of it is Yiddish. The talks are mainly stories of earlier Rebbes and chassidim, memories of Lubavitch, and calls to strengthen Tomchei Temimim, chassidic minyanim and prayer. The aim is to wake up American Jews, and descendants of chassidim who have drifted, through memory, stories and the "essential light" of Chassidus.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: SO · Sha'arei Orah
abstract: What it is. Discourses for Chanukah and Purim. The author's introduction states the aim: to 'light up the soul with the Divine light' ('the way of life'), so that each reader 'may find rest for his soul according to his measure'. The book is built on two kinds of mesirus nefesh (giving one's life for what matters most) and two kinds of light. Chanukah is light from below, from the receiver: the soul's own lamp. Purim is light from above, from the giver, as at Sinai.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: Suffering and loss
abstract: ## C14 · Depression or mental illness, in me or someone I love I've lost all desire, even for my wife and children. Or: someone I love has broken down mentally and the doctors give no hope. What do we do? What is really going on. The evidence is thin, and this entry keeps to it.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: SY · Sheeris Yehudah
abstract: What it is. A collection of halachic writings: a commentary on the laws of salting meat, then responsa on all four parts of the Shulchan Aruch (many exchanged with the Tzemach Tzedek), the agunah files, notes on the Gemara and teachings heard from the Alter Rebbe. It has no maamarim and no teaching on avodah or bittul. Its human material comes up in passing, in how a posek treats people: a shochet restored through real teshuvah, a frightened woman believed, agunos released, peace kept between husband and wife.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: TAN · Tanya (Likkutei Amarim, Shaar HaYichud VehaEmunah, Iggeres HaTeshuvah, Iggeres HaKodesh)
abstract: What it is. A handbook for the "beinoni", the in-between person: someone whose evil still has its full strength inside but never gets to rule his deeds, speech or thought. Likkutei Amarim maps the two souls and gives a graded method: contemplation that produces love and awe, rules of timing for sadness and bitterness, and ways to handle intrusive thoughts, pride and love of others. Iggeres HaTeshuvah redefines return as leaving the sin, not fasting.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: TC1 · Toras Chaim
abstract: What it is. This part is a set of long, closely argued maamarim on the Bereishis and Noach portions. Each one starts from a verse or a saying of the Sages and works it out through Kabbalistic structure: Tohu and Tikun, the divine names Ma and Ban, chochmah and the middos, the four worlds. Now and then it grounds the abstraction in the inner work of the heart, mostly prayer, teshuvah and bittul.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: TC2 · Toras Chaim
abstract: What it is. A collection of long, systematic maamarim on the Genesis portions from Toldos to Vayechi. Its subjects are the wells Yitzchak dug, Leah and Rachel, Yaakov and Esav, Yosef's sheaves, the cupbearer's grapes, and Yehudah's vine. Each is explained in Kabbalistic terms: chesed and gevurah, tohu and tikkun, Ma and Ban, the raising and refining of fallen sparks. Woven into this, often in parentheses, are sharp observations about the service of the heart: how joy, bitterness, contemplation, prayer and repentance work, and how they go wrong.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: TC3 · Toras Chaim
abstract: What it is. Maamarim of the Mitteler Rebbe on Shemos, Va'era, Bo, Beshalach and Pesach (1821-1826). The frame is Kabbalistic: Egypt is the constriction of the Mochin, Pharaoh is the 'back of the neck' of the husk, and Pesach is a leap. Running through it is a sustained reading of exile as a state of the soul. Exile means the mind knowing God while the heart feels nothing. It means the whole inner self being eaten up by earning a living.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: TC4 · Toras Chaim (Shemos, vol. 2: Yisro to Pekudei)
abstract: What it is. Long maamarim on the parshiyos from Yisro to Pekudei. They are dense Kabbalistic exposition: ratzo and shov, Malchus rising and descending, nahar dinur, Amalek as a kelipah, and delight clothed in its opposite. But the Mitteler Rebbe keeps grounding each structure in what "we see with our senses" in a person.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: The Works · Tier A
abstract: A handbook for the "beinoni", the in-between person: someone whose evil still has its full strength inside but never gets to rule his deeds, speech or thought. Likkutei Amarim maps the two souls and gives a graded method: contemplation that produces love and awe, rules of timing for sadness and bitterness, and ways to handle intrusive thoughts, pride and love of others. Iggeres HaTeshuvah redefines return as leaving the sin, not fasting.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: Thought and attention
abstract: ## C11 · Stray thoughts flood my mind, above all in prayer The moment I start praying, my head fills with junk: lust, money, grudges. When my mind is idle they pour in. My attention scatters across a hundred small things and I can't gather myself. What is really going on. The works treat stray thoughts in prayer as normal, not a verdict. Tanya: a thought arising is no sin, turning from it keeps a commandment, and sadness over it is hidden pride.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: Tier B · The Rebbeim's letters and talks on everyday problems
abstract: I checked all 63 Rebbeim-tier candidates, opening context where it mattered. 55 are supported, 8 only partly, and none fail outright. Most important fixes: (1) envy_points_the_way misreads B18:Q14. In the Tzemach Tzedek's reading (Igros Kodesh line 74555), holy envy is a 'holy worm' that rots the animal soul's traits, which is a good thing, not the envier.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: TO1 · Torah Ohr
abstract: What it is. Maamarim on the weekly portions, delivered by the Alter Rebbe and edited by the Tzemach Tzedek. Each one starts from a verse or a saying of the Sages, builds a Kabbalistic account of the worlds (sefirot, Tohu and Tikun, the surrounding and indwelling light), and then often turns briefly to avodah: prayer, the Shema, Torah study, bitterness and joy, refining one's traits.

family: The medicine map: the Chabad library read for everyday problems
title: TO2 · Torah Ohr
abstract: What it is. Maamarim the Alter Rebbe gave on the weekly portions from Beshalach to Vayakhel, plus Purim maamarim on Megillat Esther and later additions. Each one opens on a verse or a teaching of the Sages, builds a Kabbalistic structure (the Name Havaya, Chochmah and Binah, sparks, kelipot), and then usually turns in a paragraph or two to avodah: prayer, Shema, bitterness and joy, humility, and love of G-d.

family: The integration map: how the unity becomes a person's nature
title: The integration map: how the unity of G-d becomes a person's nature
abstract: The books do not ask a person to believe the unity of G-d harder; they ask him to hold it, because in Chassidus to know (da'at) is to bind the mind to a truth until it is as real as a thing you see. So the path starts before the thinking: a quiet place, worries set down, the yoke of Heaven accepted, a coin given, a little learning, and a heart that is open and glad, not heavy.

family: Transformation: a framework and forty-seven ways in
title: The transformation framework
abstract: The owner: the goal is to bring people closer to G-d, not the G-d of dogma but the Chassidic one, found within yourself: a path to the true self, using the method of Chassidus. So this framework is built as one road. Each session moves a person one step closer to who they really are, down through the layers to the point where the self at its root and what gives it being turn out to be one (ST10), and then back up into an ordinary day carrying it (ST12 …

family: Transformation: a framework and forty-seven ways in
title: The technique library: forty-seven ways in, for anyone
abstract: What this is. Forty-seven real meditative and contemplative techniques, each taken from a Chabad or wider Chassidic practice, restated so anyone can do them without belief, and specified for a live session: the exact lines the guide speaks, the silence after each line, a one-tap check-in, and what to do for each answer. Each also has a second script for someone who believes in G-d, wherever the wording differs.

family: Transformation: a framework and forty-seven ways in
title: Only One: the transformation cards
abstract: The guide should not only know what Chassidus says. It should know what a teaching is trying to do to perception, and how to help someone test that shift without forcing it. Each card stores one such shift: the sentence a person starts from, the Chassidic distinction that answers it, the perception it aims at, one operation attention can do in about ten seconds, right now in the chat, and what the guide must never do with it.

family: How a conversation creates change
title: How a conversation creates change
abstract: This is craft, not content. The content stays Chassidus. We borrow mechanisms from research on brief help, chat agents, the helping relationship, memory and planning. The owner's rules stand (claims.md D1 to D44): outside danger the guide never refers to therapy, doctors or medication; no breathing drills, body scans or relaxation; danger overrides everything; universal for anyone (D17, D28). It builds on what we have. ../conversation/research-counseling.md already covers empathy, the alliance meta-analysis, MITI reflections and questions, the righting reflex and the AI template. This file does not repeat it.

family: How a conversation creates change
title: The mechanism map: how each Chassidic process of change works on a person
abstract: What it is. For each core Chassidic process of change: what the sources say it is, which psychological mechanisms it probably works through, how good the evidence for each mechanism is, the conversational move that engages that mechanism, who should not get it, and where the psychology and the teaching part ways. What it is not. It is not the guide's vocabulary. The guide never names these constructs, never refers to therapy outside danger, uses no breathing drills, body scans or relaxation, and never recommends drink (owner's rules, claims.md).

family: How a conversation creates change
title: Safety and contraindications of the translation layer
abstract: This file asks one question of every teaching and practice the guide uses: where can it hurt, and how? It gives, for each risk, the mechanism, the evidence and its strength, the Chassidic guard where the sources already have one, the signs as they would show up in a chat message, what the guide must never do, and what it does instead.

family: How a conversation creates change
title: Rubric for the simulated-client panel
abstract: For each scenario, run the simulator (instructions in scenarios.json) against the guide as deployed: conversation core, cards, page reply checks. Three runs per scenario, different seeds. Save each as eval/runs/<version>/<scenario-id>-<run>.md, with the guide's session log (card ids, the A1 codes, the A4 code) appended. Strip anything that names the guide version. Shuffle. Two LLM judges from different model families score every transcript with this rubric; one human with clinical training scores all crisis transcripts (crisis-1, crisis-2, shame-1) and a random half of the rest.

family: How a conversation creates change
title: The guide's persona: a healing, meditative presence built from the sources
abstract: A mashpia's stance, not a mashpia. The sources on guiding say: sit lower, no authority, no display of learning; the person is the purpose; at most a cause, never the healer; they should leave able to go on without you (constitution, WHO YOU ARE: T35, TH-28, RAF-09, RAF-19, RAF-46; darkei-hachassidus/DARKEI-HACHASSIDUS.md on the mashpia and the farbrengen). The guide never calls itself a rav, a mashpia, a therapist or a friend, and never claims love, memory or secrecy it doesn't have (translation-layer/SAFETY.md, R15).

family: How a conversation creates change
title: The mechanics of proven therapies, borrowed for a chat guide
abstract: Borrowed moves, never referrals, never protocols. The guide never names a therapy to the person, never suggests seeing a therapist outside danger, and never runs a clinical protocol (imagery rescripting, chair work, parts dialogues, exposure hierarchies, trauma processing). What it borrows is the small conversational act that the research says carries change: a juxtaposition, a reflection, one Socratic question, a scheduled time, a small act tied to a cue. Psychology describes, Chassidus teaches. A therapy's evidence says a move tends to change people.

family: How a conversation creates change
title: Therapies that already join faith and psychology
abstract: Track 3 of the translation layer. The question: people have already built therapies that put faith and psychology together. What did they find helps, what did they find harms, how do they speak to religious and non-religious people, and what should "Only One" take from them? Contents 1. The short answer 2. David Rosmarin: trust and mistrust in G-d, the bitachon trial, SPIRIT, the books 3. The special question: trust in G-d, worry and intolerance of uncertainty 4. Kenneth Pargament: religious coping, spiritual struggles, spiritually integrated psychotherapy 5.

family: The mashal: how the Rebbeim make an analogy, and new ones for today
title: The laws of the mashal
abstract: R. Aharon of Strashelye wrote down, as fixed law, what his teacher the Alter Rebbe did case by case. A mashal is a handle on a basket: it gives the mind a grip on what it cannot hold, and the basket is what matters. It has three conditions. First, only someone who holds the teaching from its root may make a mashal for it; meshalim are found, not invented, and the deeper one stands, the more and the further the meshalim.

family: The mashal: how the Rebbeim make an analogy, and new ones for today
title: METHOD: how the Rebbeim make a mashal, and how to make a new one
abstract: Where the Rebbeim look. The king (65 of 388), craft and building (46), the body (37), father and child (35), the soul's own powers of speech, thought and will (30), and nature (30) make up two thirds of all meshalim. Sun and light, water, fire, commerce and teacher follow. Music, food, travel and love are rare. Counting every domain an entry names, nature and the body rise (49 and 45): many meshalim join a human scene to a natural one. From my flesh.

family: The mashal: how the Rebbeim make an analogy, and new ones for today
title: NEW: new meshalim for today
abstract: Start with the plain version. Use the full mashal only when the person leans in. - Always say the break, at least in one line, when the teaching is about what G-d is. The break is part of the mashal, not a footnote. - After it lands, put the picture down and say the point plainly (PR-L10). - Read for whom and risk before using a mashal with someone in pain.

family: The mashal: how the Rebbeim make an analogy, and new ones for today
title: SB1: Source book of meshalim I (Tanya, the Alter Rebbe, the Mitteler Rebbe, R. Aharon)
abstract: Source book I: 199 meshalim from the Tanya (all five parts), Torah Or and Likkutei Torah, the Mitteler Rebbe (Shaar HaYichud, Imrei Binah, Toras Chaim, Sha'arei Orah, Kuntres HaHitpa'alut, with Pirush HaMilos, Derech Chaim, Maamarei Admur HaEmtzai, Sha'arei Teshuvah, Ner Mitzvah VeTorah Or) and R. Aharon's Shaarei HaYichud VeHaEmunah. Each has its parts matched to the subject, where it breaks (30 stated in the text, 169 ours), R. Aharon's principles it shows, a verified Hebrew source, recurrences, and a plain rendering.

abstract: Strand SB2 of the meshalim project (see BRIEF.md). Companion data: sb2.json. Principles: PRINCIPLES.md / principles.json (ids PR-L01 to PR-L15). What is here. 189 meshalim, one entry per mashal per author (a mashal that two authors use gets an entry under each only when each uses it differently; otherwise it is listed under 'recurs'). By author: Baal Shem Tov 30, Maggid of Mezritch 24, Tzemach Tzedek 28, Rebbe Maharash 16, Rebbe Rashab 38, Rebbe Rayatz 18, the Rebbe 17, Piaseczner Rebbe 18.

abstract: The machine-readable twin is sources.json: an array of {id, name, what, how, why, when, not_when, quotes:[{he,en,work,file,line,ocr}], whose, chat}. Entry T-S17 also carries examples, the 19 verified lines of the Piaseczner's voice. Where the sources speak most directly about teaching: - Alter Rebbe. Tanya, Compiler's Foreword (why a book instead of yechidus; each reader "according to his way"). Iggeret HaKodesh 15 (the father who shrinks his wisdom for his son). Iggeret HaKodesh 22 (no counsel in material matters). - Mitteler Rebbe.

family: The teacher: how Chassidus is imparted
title: The Baal Shem Tov: how he met people, and how the guide can carry his manner
abstract: What this is. His manner of meeting a person (Part 1), his voice (Part 2), voice rules for the guide (Part 3), how he receives you at the door (Part 4), six sample exchanges (Part 5), 25 of his parables and stories as tools (Part 6), and guards (Part 7). Then honest limits. What it builds on.

family: The teacher: how Chassidus is imparted
title: The four teachers: how they present and teach
abstract: What this is. How four teachers present a teaching: the shape of a talk or a piece, their signature moves, how they speak to the listener, how they meet pain and doubt, what the guide should take, and what it should not copy. Then where they agree, where they differ, and the teacher Only One should be. What it builds on. Rabbi Moshe Weinberger/DIGEST-WEINBERGER.md and HOW-THEY-MEET-A-SEEKER.md, Rav Joey Rosenfeld/DIGEST.md, Rav Yitzchak Meir Morgenstern/DIGEST.md. Those give what each teaches. This file gives how.

family: The teacher: how Chassidus is imparted
title: The teacher: how a guide imparts the wisdom, moment by moment, in a chat
abstract: Good one-to-one teaching is mostly getting the learner to do the thinking. The best tutors ask, hint and wait more than they explain; students learn from what they construct (Chi et al. 2001; Chi & Wylie 2014). For hisbonenus this is not a style choice: the binding of the mind is the person's own act. The teacher's skill is reading the last message and choosing the smallest move.

family: The universal translation: the unity of G-d for anyone
title: The universal translation: the unity of G-d for anyone, anywhere
abstract: The owner's question: "We have the brain to explain the ideas. Now, how do we make it relevant to ANYBODY in the world, any situation, any background? How is the integration of the unity of G-d translated for anybody?" The answer in one paragraph. The Rebbe already designed the universal translation, and argued for it in public for years: the moment of silence. One minute, the same for every child, Jewish or not. The content is fixed: the Creator and Ruler of the world, an eye that sees.

family: The universal translation: the unity of G-d for anyone
title: The plain-experience lexicon
abstract: The owner: "The main issue is figuring out a way to communicate the essence of Chassidus to somebody without it sounding like Chassidus." Even the project's own universal wording ("the source of all being", "given its being", "the oneness", "the Essence") sounds religious or philosophical to most ears. This file says 69 core insights of Chassidus in the language of ordinary experience, so that a person recognises each one from their own life before any concept or name appears.

family: The universal translation: the unity of G-d for anyone
title: Only One: a universal framework for the unity of G-d
abstract: This is the unity of G-d as Chassidus teaches it, laid out as one picture of reality and of the self that any person can test in their own life, and as a map of what changes in a life when it is known. It feeds "Only One", the guide that walks a person inward one quiet step at a time.

family: The ladder from zero
title: How modern teachers map the inner path
abstract: The modern books that work all share one format, and the format is separable from their content. Every stage gets: A name you can remember and say about yourself ("I'm in Stage 4"). A one-line goal. What it feels like from inside, described plainly, so you recognize it. The skill being trained (one, not five). The practice: how long, which steps, what to do when. The obstacles, each named, each with its fix. Signs of mastery: how you know you can move on.
